In-house precedent verified in this repo: games/bastion-realms/runtime/data/achievements.js ships 19 achievements, and games/dungeon-forge/runtime/net/cloud.js runs a Supabase REST leaderboard on the same project and anon key Last Circle already uses (net.js:22-23) — so neither an achievement list nor an online leaderboard is new infrastructure here.
strengths: A persistent meta exists at all and is surfaced in three places — the in-HUD XP bar + challenge card (hud.js showHUD), the menu level/XP/career strip (hud.js:~560-580), and the post-match XP+career line. Most browser 3D shooters ship with zero meta; the menu strip in particular means the game shows evidence you have played it before you press anything.
Levels pay actual rewards and the banner names them: `levelUpSub` announces the specific skin unlocked, or the next skin and the level it arrives at, so the bar is not decoration.

Challenge evaluation is honest. All three challenges are polled independently every frame rather than only the current card, so a player who dies at 2:30 with four kills still banks the elimination and damage objectives — and the whole loop is gated on `W.player.alive`, so a spectating corpse cannot farm 'Survive 3 minutes' or 'Reach the final 10' while dead.

Practice mode is correctly excluded from both XP and career (hud.js addXP/recordMatch early-return on `W.mode === 'practice'`) — the sandbox has a no-death dummy with unlimited damage, so this closes the single most obvious farm.
QUIT TO MENU routes through `W.endMatch(false)` rather than dumping straight to the menu, so a ragequit still banks the match's XP and career stats. Easy to get wrong; they got it right.

PLAY AGAIN requeues directly into a fresh match without rebuilding the cinematic menu world or re-reading the skin GLBs. Time-to-next-match is the single most important retention control in a BR and it is already correct.
Career picks the right two vanity numbers for the genre — best placement and top-10 count — rather than only kills.

gaps.gap: No daily reset of any kind — nothing about the game changes because it is a new day
gaps.evidence: The only persisted keys are `lc_progress`, `lc_skin`, `lc_seen_intro`, `lc_settings` (grep of localStorage across runtime/). `pickChallenges` is called from `showHUD` (hud.js:1192), so challenges are regenerated per MATCH, never per day. There is no date stamp, no streak counter, no first-win-of-the-day bonus, no reset countdown anywhere in the codebase.
gaps.recommendation: Add `lc_daily` keyed on the UTC date: three challenges drawn from an expanded pool that persist across matches within the day, plus a 'First win of the day: +750 XP' bonus and a 'Resets in HH:MM' countdown on the menu. The challenge structs and the live `addXP` path already exist — this is bookkeeping on top of them, not new machinery. Benchmark: ZombsRoyale.io ships 3 dailies per 24h plus 6 sets of 7 weeklies (verified).

gaps.gap: The reward table ends at level 10 — all progression content is exhausted in roughly 4-6 hours, then levels pay literally nothing
gaps.evidence: MENU_SKINS has 5 entries with unlockLevel 1, 1, 3, 6, 10 (hud.js:119-124) — only three items are earnable. Cumulative XP to level 10 = 32,400 (sum of `800 + (l-1)*700` for l=1..9). At ~730 XP for an average standard match that is ~45 matches; at ~1,500 for a strong one, ~22. Past level 10 `levelUpSub` returns the string 'RANK UP', so the level-up banner fires for a reward that does not exist.
gaps.recommendation: Extend to a ~30-tier track using rewards that need zero new art: material-tint variants of the 5 existing GLBs, callsign titles that render in the kill feed and on the post-match card, crosshair and parachute colours, and a named rank badge every 5 levels. All code-only, all appropriate for a browser build. Do not build a paid pass — the free track is the retention object.

gaps.gap: No leaderboard, despite the exact infrastructure already shipping in a sibling game in this repo
gaps.evidence: Nothing in runtime/ writes a score anywhere; grep for leaderboard/achievement across the game returns only the element-registry comment. Meanwhile net.js:22-23 already holds the Supabase URL + anon key, and games/dungeon-forge/runtime/net/cloud.js already runs a Supabase REST leaderboard against that same project. ZombsRoyale.io (verified) ranks players on eliminations-per-match and time-survived.
gaps.recommendation: One table `lc_scores` (name, kills, placement, damage, ts) written on match end, a rolling 7-day window, top 50 rendered on the menu, and a personal-best row. Copy the graceful-degradation pattern from dungeon-forge's Cloud class — if the table is unreachable it silently falls back to a local best, so the game never breaks.

gaps.gap: Progress is localStorage-only: a cache clear wipes the career and nothing crosses devices
gaps.evidence: `saveProgress` writes only `localStorage.setItem('lc_progress', ...)` (hud.js:~1142); there is no export, no import, no account, no server row. CrazyGames states the requirement explicitly: 'Players care A LOT about their progress in games, and expect their progress to synchronize across their devices', and requires the Data module, a custom backend, or automatic save unless progress is not applicable — Last Circle as shipped would not satisfy it.
gaps.recommendation: Generate a player UUID on first run, persist the same `lc_progress` blob to a Supabase row keyed on it (same anon key already in net.js), and expose a copyable 'transfer code' in Settings so a player can move their career to another browser or machine. Local stays authoritative; cloud is a mirror, so offline play is unaffected.

gaps.gap: 'Survived' time and its XP term count time spent SPECTATING, inflating the stat, the payout and the lifetime career
gaps.evidence: `timeS: Math.round(W.t)` in buildPostMatch (ffg_royale3d.js:346) is match wall-clock at the moment endMatch runs, and `W.t` keeps advancing after you die — the frame loop only stops it on `phase === 'over'` (ffg_royale3d.js:366), while dying leaves you in the supported spectate flow with its own spectator bar. Die at 0:45 of a 12:55 standard match, watch to the end, and the post-match card reads 'Survived 12:55', the formula pays 775/4 = 193 XP for it, and `career.timeAliveS += 775` (hud.js:1159). The per-match challenges are correctly guarded on `W.player.alive`; this end-of-match path is not.
gaps.recommendation: Read the real elimination time instead of W.t — `Match.eliminate` already stamps it into `this.feed` (royale.js:502), so the number is recorded and just needs to be looked up by victim id (fall back to W.t for the winner). Near-zero-cost fix in the generator, and it makes 'Survived' and career.timeAliveS true.

gaps.gap: The challenge pool is 5 entries and two of them appear in every single match
gaps.evidence: `pickChallenges` (hud.js:1192-1197) always returns CHAL_POOL[0] 'Survive 3 minutes' and CHAL_POOL[1] 'Get 1 elimination', plus one of three rotating on `level % 3`. A player has seen the entire system by their third match, and the third slot only changes when they level up.
gaps.recommendation: Expand the pool to ~25 objectives spanning weapon class ('3 shotgun eliminations'), distance ('a kill past 120m'), precision ('5 headshots'), looting ('open 6 chests', 'land a supply drop'), survival ('take zero storm damage'), and placement, then draw 3 per day without repeating the previous day's set. The struct is a label + goal + xp + `prog(W)` closure over counters that already exist — each new entry is one line.

gaps.gap: No career/stats screen, and two tracked lifetime stats are displayed nowhere
gaps.evidence: `career.damage` and `career.timeAliveS` are accumulated in recordMatch (hud.js:1158-1159) and never read by any render path — grep finds no other reference. Nothing computes win rate or K/D from the matches/wins/kills that ARE stored, and there is no per-map or per-weapon breakdown despite both being known at kill time.
gaps.recommendation: A CAREER panel off the menu: win rate, K/D, average placement, total damage, total time alive, best placement, top-10s — every one derivable from data already persisted — plus per-map win counts and a favourite-weapon row (add two counter objects to CAREER0). This is the cheapest 'reason to open the menu' in the list.

gaps.gap: No persistent player identity — you are 'You' in your own kill feed
gaps.evidence: `playerName: 'You'` is in the settings defaults (ffg_royale3d.js:420) but grep of hud.js finds no field that edits it anywhere in Settings; net.js:117 works around this by substituting 'Player-' + a random suffix online.
gaps.recommendation: A callsign field in Settings persisted with the rest of `lc_settings`, rendered in the kill feed, the post-match card and the leaderboard. Self-representation is a standard low-cost retention hook and it also removes the awkward 'Player-XYZ' fallback online.

gaps.gap: The menu advertises 'SEASON 1 · FREE TO PLAY' and there is no season
gaps.evidence: hud.js:499 renders the literal string 'SEASON 1  ·  FREE TO PLAY' in the top chrome bar. There is no season length, no end date, no seasonal reset, no seasonal reward, and no season identifier in `lc_progress`.
gaps.recommendation: Either drop the label, or make it true by putting the extended tier track behind it with a visible end date and a season-over recap ('Season 1: 62 matches, 9 wins, reached tier 24'). A dated season is one of the few reasons a lapsed browser player comes back on a specific day; an undated one is just chrome.

gaps.gap: Match XP is banked only at endMatch, so a mid-match tab close loses everything except challenge XP
gaps.evidence: The kills/damage/placement/victory/time formula runs once inside showPostMatch (hud.js:2240) and calls addXP there. Challenge XP, by contrast, already flows through `addXP` live during the match, and addXP calls saveProgress on every award — so the incremental-persist pattern exists and is simply not used for kills.
gaps.recommendation: Award and persist ~100 XP at the instant of each elimination (subtract it from the end-of-match total so nothing double-counts). It removes the all-or-nothing feel of a long standard match and it is the same one-line call the challenge path already makes.

gaps.gap: The flagship mode is the least efficient way to progress, and one standard match is longer than a top-quartile browser session
gaps.evidence: Standard storm runs 775s (12:55) vs quick's 239s (~4:00) (royale.js STORM_PHASES), but the XP formula is identical for both and only the `timeS/4` term scales with match length. Worked comparison: die at #20 with 1 kill and 250 damage — standard at 5:00 pays 405 + 325 challenge = 730 XP (~146/min); quick at 2:30 pays ~367 + 175 = 542 XP (~217/min). GameAnalytics 2024 puts the median session at 5-6 minutes and the top quartile at 8-9 — a full standard match exceeds a top-quartile session before it banks anything.
gaps.recommendation: Apply a mode multiplier (~1.6x) to standard's match XP so the flagship mode is also the efficient one, and pair it with the incremental kill-XP fix above so a long match pays out continuously rather than only at the end. Do not shorten standard — 12:55 is a deliberate, correct pacing decision; fix the reward rate instead.

verdict: The loot model is a careful, correctly-executed Fortnite derivative — 5 slots, a 5-tier rarity ladder, Fortnite's exact healing table, seeded deterministic placement that lets multiplayer skip item sync entirely — and on structure it is at parity with a polished browser BR. The gaps are not in the model but in its edges: the entire consumable category is healing (no throwables at all), a started heal is an uncancellable no-shoot lock that already spent the item, chests make no sound until you open them, and the one line of UI that tells you what E does lies to you whenever your inventory is full.
what_last_circle_does:
RARITY: 5 tiers (common→legendary), `RARITY_DMG_MULT = [1.0,1.08,1.16,1.24,1.32]` and `RARITY_SPREAD_MULT = [1.0,0.9,0.81,0.73,0.66]` (sim/royale.js:48-49) — legendary = +32% damage, -34% spread. Rarity changes nothing else (mag comes from `K.WEAPONS[id].mag` regardless — loot.js:431).

DROP RATES: `LOOT_WEIGHTS` (royale.js:289-293) floor [40,30,18,9,3], chest [15,30,30,18,7], supply [0,0,10,35,55]. `rollFloorItem` (royale.js:437-449) = 45% weapon / 25% ammo / 30% consumable; weapon type weights pistol 16, smg 22, ar 24, shotgun 20, sniper 10, glauncher 8. `rollChest` = 1 gun + 2 ammo boxes for it + (55% a consumable | 45% 20 more ammo) ≈ 3 items. `rollSupplyDrop` = 1 gun from [0,5,30,20,25,20] at supply rarity (55% legendary) + big_shield x2 + medkit x1 + 3 ammo boxes.

PLACEMENT: `populate()` (loot.js:76-98) spawns an item at each floor point with p=0.55 in standard (`0.55 * min(1.6, lootMult)`; quick mode lootMult 1.8 → p=0.88 plus a 40% second item). Maps are 1600 m square (maps.js:37) with 130 wilderness floor points each 12% to also carry a chest (maps.js:1058-1064); every hut is a floor point + 50% chest (maps.js:545-546); towers/barns/ships/sky-islands/volcano rim get guaranteed roof or high-ground chests. Placement is seeded (`mulberry32(W.seed ^ 0x100f)`) and ids are derived from source not spawn order ("f:"+i, "cb:"+chestId+":"+i, "dd:"+victimId+":"+k) so clients agree with no item sync.

INVENTORY: 5 slots, slot 0 pre-filled with a common pistol; ammo is a separate reserve dict (player.js:58-65). `START_LOADOUT` = pistol + 36 light. `GUN_CAP = 3` (loot.js:357) — walkover refuses a 4th gun, so a kitted player is 3 guns + at most 2 consumable stacks (i.e. 2 of the 4 heal types). Ammo caps light 300 / medium 240 / shells 60 / heavy 36 / grenades 20, boxes 24/20/8/6/4 (royale.js:84-90). No manual drop key exists — `KeyE` is the only loot input (player.js:470), `dropItem()` is internal to swap/trade-up.

INTERACTION: walkover auto-pickup inside 1.5 m, hint radius 2.4 m (loot.js:570-577); tap E = swap the floor item into the ACTIVE slot; HOLD E 2.0 s on a chest (`CHEST_OPEN_S = 2.0`) with a conic-gradient progress ring (hud.js:1490-1494). `wouldAccept`/`give` now correctly return false at ammo and consumable caps so over-cap items stay on the floor.

HEALING: `CONSUMABLES` (royale.js:94-99) bandage 15 hp / cap 75 / 3 s / stack 15; medkit 100 / cap 100 / 8 s / stack 3; mini_shield 25 / cap 50 / 2 s / stack 6; big_shield 50 / cap 100 / 4 s / stack 3. Shield starts at 0 (player.js:56), so 200 EHP is entirely potion-earned. `HEAL = {speedMult: 0.45, blocksSprint: true}` and firing is blocked while `a.healing` (weapons.js:324). Every consumable is a heal — there is no throwable, no utility, no armour item.

SUPPLY DROPS: max 2 per match, first at storm phase ≥2, ≥3 phases apart (loot.js:241-242), balloon falls at 9 m/s from y=200 into a point inside the NEXT circle (`nextRadius * 0.6 * rng`), bursts into 4 item stacks, with map marker + "SUPPLY DROP · LEGENDARY LOOT INBOUND" announce.

DEATH DROP: entire kit — every carried weapon including the equipped one, every consumable stack, and each ammo type above 8 (loot.js:521-538), seeded off the victim id so every client spawns identical drops.
what_benchmarks_do:
FINAL DROP (primary bar) — only partly verifiable. Confirmed from crazygames.com/game/final-drop and final-drop.com: up to 100 players, browser, has building and material harvesting, controls "1–6 = select item" (six inventory slots), "E = use item / interact (hold)", "R = reload". Its rarity tiers, chest tables, supply-drop rules, shield values and drop key are NOT publicly documented — I could not verify them and am not going to invent them. Every Final Drop loot-internals claim below is labelled unverified.

FORTNITE (verified via Pro Game Guides / Fortnite Wiki / gamepressure): Shield Potion 5 s, +50 shield to 100 cap, 2 per slot. Small Shield Potion 2 s, +25 to a 50 cap, drops in 3s, max stack 6. Bandages 4 s, +15 to a 75 cap, max stack 15. Med Kit 10 s, full heal, max stack 3. Weapon rarity is a shallow ladder: Ranger AR 30/31/33/35/36 across common→legendary, i.e. +20% total (Fortnite Wiki). 5 inventory slots with ammo and mats tracked separately; consumable slots are contested between heals and throwables (grenades, shockwaves, launch pads); items can be dropped manually with a quantity picker; picking up while full shows a "Swap" prompt naming the outgoing item; chests emit the well-known proximity jingle before you see them; rarity beams/pillars mark ground loot.

APEX (verified via Apex Legends Wiki / esports.gg): grid backpack sized by rarity — Level 1 = 12 slots, L2 = 14, L3/L4 = 16, with L4 halving heal apply time; two weapon slots; armour and healing are separate item classes; three dedicated grenade slots; starter kit is 4 Syringes + 4 Shield Cells.

PUBG/WARZONE: weight- or slot-based inventory with attachments and tiered armour — a heavier model than a browser BR should copy, and not a fair parity target here.

Where the benchmarks agree and Last Circle can be judged: (a) the consumable category is never 100% healing, (b) a heal in progress can always be cancelled, (c) full-inventory pickup prompts name the outgoing item, (d) manual drop exists, (e) chests announce themselves audibly, (f) loot rarity is readable at distance via beams.
strengths: Seeded deterministic loot with source-derived ids ('f:'+i, 'cb:'+chestId+':'+i, 'dd:'+victimId+':'+k, 'sd:'+n+':'+i) means multiplayer needs no item-state replication at all — only take/open mirroring plus a join-sync of taken/opened id lists (loot.js:63-69). For a Supabase-Realtime browser BR that is a genuinely strong architectural call, and it is the reason the loot layer has none of the desync classes that usually plague browser BRs.

The healing table is Fortnite's, verified number-for-number (15/75, 100/100, 25/50, 50/100 with stacks 15/3/6/3) with browser-appropriate speed-ups (bandage 3 s vs 4, medkit 8 s vs 10, big shield 4 s vs 5). This is proven tuning adopted deliberately rather than invented, and the bandage 75-HP cap preserves the correct 'you need a medkit to top off' tension.

Everyone spawns armed — START_LOADOUT pistol + 36 light ammo (royale.js:92), with the code comment naming the intent ('a BR shooter, not a scavenger sim'). This removes the single worst onboarding failure for a browser audience: the unarmed 30-second scramble. Combined with the auto-equip that switches you off the starter common pistol on your first real pickup (loot.js:440), the first 60 seconds always has a gun in your hands.

Over-cap loot destruction is now correctly closed on BOTH paths: give() returns false at the ammo reserve cap (loot.js:424) and at a full consumable stack (loot.js:484), so items you cannot carry stay on the floor instead of vanishing with a fake pickup toast. That is the behaviour Fortnite and Apex ship and it is now matched.

Death drops the ENTIRE kit — every carried weapon including the equipped one, every consumable stack, and each ammo type above 8 (loot.js:529-537) — seeded off the victim id so all clients spawn identical loot. The kill-to-loot loop, which is the actual engine of BR mid-game, works and works in multiplayer.

Supply-drop pacing is designed, not thrown in: max 2 per match, first at storm phase >= 2, minimum 3 phases apart (loot.js:241-242), and crucially the crate targets the NEXT circle (st.nextCenter, radius * 0.6) so it never lands behind the wall. Plus an inbound announce, a persistent map marker, and a landed cue. That is the AAA behaviour, at browser cost.

Rarity is communicated by colour AND a Roman numeral I-V on the slot (hud.js:1693-1698) with an explicit comment about colour-vision deficiency. Fortnite is hue-only. This is one of the few places where Last Circle is genuinely ahead of its AAA reference.

Chest opening is a 2.0 s hold channel with a conic-gradient progress ring — a real commitment window with a visible tell, rather than Fortnite's near-instant interact. Bots obey the same 2 s channel (bots.js:435-438), so the rule is universal rather than a player-only tax.

Bots are full participants in the loot economy: they use the same wouldAccept/give/openChest pipeline, and botWouldTradeUp (loot.js:381-390) scores rarity first then DPS so a bot at the 3-gun cap trades up and drops its worst gun. Without it the GUN_CAP would have frozen 49 of 50 actors on 'starter pistol + first two guns I touched' and made every chest roll in the lobby worthless.

Loot queries run on a 24 m spatial hash (LOOT_CELL = 24, loot.js:19-27) with squared-distance compares, and the bob/spin and chest-glow updates are distance-culled at 90 m / 160 m. That is what makes 49 bots calling nearbyLoot() per frame affordable, and it is the kind of thing that usually gets skipped and then tanks the frame rate at match start.

Weapon slot icons are live 3D thumbnails rendered from the actual view-model protos through a dedicated 96x72 offscreen renderer and cached (hud.js:1595-1631), with consumables falling back to legible emoji glyphs. The inventory bar reads as a shipped product, not a placeholder.

gaps.gap: There are no throwables or utility items — the entire consumable category is healing, so every inventory decision is 'which heal', never 'heal vs utility'
gaps.evidence: CONSUMABLES (sim/royale.js:94-99) contains exactly bandage, medkit, mini_shield, big_shield. WEAPON_IDS (royale.js:66) has glauncher but no hand-thrown item; give() only handles kind weapon/ammo/consumable (loot.js:415-506); hud.js:1726 still carries a vestigial `d.id !== "grenade"` check for an item that does not exist. Fortnite contests the same 5 slots between heals and grenades/shockwaves/launch pads; Apex gives grenades three dedicated slots.
gaps.recommendation: Add one throwable — a frag grenade — as a consumable-kind item with stack 3, thrown from the slot on fire. The whole projectile path already exists: glauncher runs speed 26, arc: true, fuseS 2.0, splashR 3.5 (royale.js:64) through splashScale(), so this is a table entry plus a throw arc, not new systems. Give it ~8% of the floor consumable weight and a slot in rollChest's consumable branch. It is the single change that turns the 5-slot inventory from a heal shelf into an actual loadout decision, and it violates none of the settled constraints.

gaps.gap: A started heal cannot be cancelled and the item is already spent — an 8 s medkit is an 8-second window where you cannot fire, with no escape and no refund
gaps.evidence: useConsumable decrements the stack at channel START (player.js:1228) then sets `a.healing = {id, tLeft: c.useS}` (player.js:1242). The only place a.healing is cleared is completion (player.js:671). equipSlot (weapons.js:189-209) does not touch a.healing, and firing is gated on `!a.healing` (weapons.js:324) — so pressing 1 to pull your AR mid-medkit swaps the model and still leaves you unable to shoot for the remaining seconds. Fortnite and Apex both cancel the channel on weapon swap and only consume the item on completion.
gaps.recommendation: Cancel on weapon-slot input and refund: in equipSlot, if `a.healing && slot.kind === "weapon"`, push the count back onto (or recreate) the consumable slot and null a.healing, emitting a healCancel event for the HUD bar. This is the correct fix rather than shortening the channels — the 45% slow + sprint lock that shipped this session is good design, but it is only fair if the commitment is escapable at the cost of the progress.

gaps.gap: Chests are silent until opened — loot discovery is purely visual, and the game has no equivalent of the chest jingle every BR player is trained on
gaps.evidence: audio.js binds chestOpened (line 314), supplyDropSpawned (324) and supplyDropLanded (313), and nothing else loot-related; there is no per-frame proximity emitter for unopened chests. Discovery is therefore entirely the glow sprite + 7 m additive beam built in spawnChest (loot.js:219-227), which the update loop culls beyond 160 m and which any terrain rise or wall occludes. The positional audio helpers already take a position and a radius — e.g. `blip(660, 0.3, 0.14, "triangle", c.pos, 40)`.
gaps.recommendation: Emit a low-rate positional shimmer for the nearest 1-2 unopened chests within ~25 m, reusing the existing blip(freq, dur, gain, type, pos, radius) signature on a ~1.2 s interval from the loot update loop (the distance cull at loot.js:556-562 already walks exactly this set). It is a handful of lines against code that exists, and it is the highest-value-per-line change in this dimension: it converts building interiors from 'walk in and look around' into 'I can hear one upstairs'.

gaps.gap: The interact prompt always reads 'Pick up' even when pressing E will throw your active slot on the ground
gaps.evidence: loot.js:603 builds the hint with no swap flag; hud.js:1486-1488 renders `"[E] " + labelFor(hint.data)` and labelFor (hud.js:1724-1727) hardcodes the string 'Pick up'. But when you are full, loot.js:601 calls `pickup(W, a, target.id, {swap: true})`, and the swap branches at loot.js:467-471 / 497-498 drop whatever occupies the active slot — your legendary AR or your entire 15-bandage stack. Fortnite's prompt flips to 'Swap' and names the outgoing item.
gaps.recommendation: The predicate already exists and is already exported: stamp the hint with `const full = !W.wouldAcceptItem(a, target.data)` plus the outgoing slot, and render '[E] Swap for X — drops Y' when full. Roughly six lines across loot.js:603 and hud.js:1488. Silent destruction of a player's heal stack is the kind of thing that ends a session, and the information to prevent it is sitting two functions away.

gaps.gap: There is no manual drop, so a loadout is decided by whatever you happened to walk over first and can never be un-decided
gaps.evidence: The only loot input bound is KeyE (player.js:470, 499); dropItem() (loot.js:509) is reachable only from the internal swap and bot trade-up paths. Walkover auto-pickup takes ANY weapon while under the cap (loot.js:575-578 only tests `gunCount() >= 3`), so three common guns grabbed in the landing scramble permanently occupy the 3 gun slots. Shedding one requires finding a floor gun, equipping the junk gun by number first, then pressing E — because the swap targets the ACTIVE slot, not the worst one. Fortnite and Apex both ship a drop key.
gaps.recommendation: Bind a drop key (G) that calls the existing dropItem() with the active slot and clears it — the function already handles the network mirror via netDropItem. Optionally make the swap smarter for guns: when the active slot is not a weapon and the incoming item is, swap against worstGunIdx() (loot.js:362-375, already written and already used by bots) instead of the active slot. Note this also unblocks the follow-on case where the GUN_CAP of 3 leaves room for only 2 of the 4 consumable types.

gaps.gap: Ground loot has no rarity beam — a legendary on the floor is a flat 1.1 m ring, and a chest deletes its own beam at the exact moment it pays out
gaps.evidence: itemMesh (loot.js:120-146) adds only rarityRing(), a `TorusGeometry(0.55, 0.05, 6, 24)` laid flat at y≈0.08 — a few pixels tall past ~15 m and occluded by any rise. Chests get the full treatment (glow sprite + 7 m additive beam, loot.js:219-227) but openChest strips all three markers (loot.js:323-325) before spawning the payout. Same for the two supply-drop legendaries (loot.js:273) and for every death drop (loot.js:527), which dumps a full 5-slot kit. Additionally, non-weapon items always draw a grey common ring — `rarityRing(data.kind === "weapon" ? data.rarity : 0)` at loot.js:122 — so a medkit and a common pistol have an identical ground signature.
gaps.recommendation: Give itemMesh a short additive beam tinted by K.RARITY_COLOR, scaled by tier (common ~1.2 m / 0.10 opacity, legendary ~3.2 m / 0.26), reusing the chest beam material verbatim and gating it behind the 90 m distance cull already in the update loop. Give consumables their own tint (green heal / blue shield) rather than the grey common ring. Rarity beams are the signature loot-readability device in every benchmark; the palette, the beam code and the cull all already exist here.

gaps.gap: Big shields strictly dominate mini shields — identical throughput, higher cap, half the slot pressure, so there is no reason to ever drink a mini
gaps.evidence: CONSUMABLES (royale.js:97-98): mini_shield 25 shield / 2 s = 12.5 shield per second; big_shield 50 / 4 s = 12.5 per second. Fortnite deliberately breaks that tie — verified small shield 25/2 s = 12.5 against shield potion 50/5 s = 10 — so minis are the rate-superior in-fight top-up and bigs are the between-fight refill. Here the two items occupy the same tactical role and one is simply better, which flattens 2 of the 4 consumable types into 1.
gaps.recommendation: Change big_shield useS from 4 to 5. One number in royale.js:98. It restores Fortnite's verified relationship (mini 12.5/s vs big 10/s), gives minis a real identity as the mid-fight sip, and makes the mini stack of 6 worth the slot it occupies.

gaps.gap: Every chest in the world rolls the same table, so no POI is worth contesting for its loot quality — only for its geometry
gaps.evidence: openChest calls K.rollChest(rng) unconditionally (loot.js:328); there is one chest weight row in LOOT_WEIGHTS ([15,30,30,18,7], royale.js:291) and lootPoints carry only {x,y,z,kind,poi} with no tier field (maps.js:522-523). Placement does encode some risk tiering — sky islands get a guaranteed chest (maps.js:1034), the volcano rim gets high-ground chests (maps.js:779-782), towers and barns get roof chests reachable only by ramp — but the reward at the top of that climb is statistically identical to a chest in a wilderness shack. Fortnite ships rare/gold chests; Apex ships Hot Zones and vaults.
gaps.recommendation: Add a `tier` field to chest() in maps.js (default 0, tier 1 for roof/sky-island/volcano-rim/ship-deck placements) and a second weight row LOOT_WEIGHTS.chest_gold, e.g. [0,10,28,37,25], selected in openChest. Tint the existing chest ring and beam gold for tier 1 so the reward is legible from the ground before the climb. This makes vertical routes and the named POIs pay for the exposure they cost, which is the whole point of high ground in a BR.

gaps.gap: The only source of legendary loot lands uncontested — the highest-value event in the match carries no risk
gaps.evidence: rollSupplyDrop is the only roll whose weights make legendary the modal outcome ([0,0,10,35,55], royale.js:292) and it fires at most twice per match. bots.js has no subscription to supplyDropSpawned or supplyDropLanded — the loot state scores just 20 mid-match once a bot is upgraded (bots.js:166) against ROTATE and ENGAGE in the 40-95 band, so a bot reaches the crate only by coincidence. The player therefore walks to both drops alone, while a 200 m balloon and a HUD announce advertise them.
gaps.recommendation: Have bots react to the landing: on supplyDropLanded, flag every alive bot within ~220 m with a supply target and force a re-think, then add an s.SUPPLY utility score that decays with distance and expires after ~90 s, routing to the existing actLoot. It is a small addition to a system that already exists, and it converts the two most valuable moments in the match from a free pickup into the contested-crate beat the BR formula is built around.

gaps.gap: Rarity moves only two numbers, so a legendary feels statistically better but not mechanically different
gaps.evidence: hitDamage applies RARITY_DMG_MULT (royale.js:399) and effectiveSpread applies RARITY_SPREAD_MULT (royale.js:156); nothing else reads rarity. Mag size comes from the base table regardless (`mag: K.WEAPONS[data.id].mag`, loot.js:431) and reloadS has no rarity term. Note the ladder is already steeper than the AAA reference — +32% damage at legendary against Fortnite's verified Ranger AR spread of 30/31/33/35/36, i.e. +20% — so the power budget is there; it is just spent on one axis.
gaps.recommendation: Redistribute rather than add: shave the damage step to +6%/tier and spend the difference on a reload multiplier (about -5%/tier) and +1 mag every second tier. A legendary AR that reloads noticeably faster reads as a different weapon in the hand, which is what makes a rarity ladder felt rather than merely tallied — and it costs no new systems, just two multipliers at the equip and reload sites.

verdict: The drop-select screen (a real map with live bot-declared contest heat) is genuinely better than anything Fortnite, Apex or PUBG ships, and the freefall/canopy split with a Warzone-style cut-and-redeploy toggle is a correct, well-built skeleton. But the two things that make a BR drop feel like a BR drop are missing: there is no aircraft — you are teleported to a point directly above your own pick, so the 26-second descent has no destination — and the canopy falls at 5.5 m/s and moves at 8.5 m/s, roughly a third of every benchmark's canopy, making the default first 26 seconds of every match an unskippable 19-second float.
what_last_circle_does: Map is 1600 m square (maps.js:23 `const SIZE = 1600`), 8-9 named POIs per map (maps.js:752-758 / 804-812 / 904-911), 50 players (sim/royale.js:284). Drop select (hud.js:906-1060): full-map canvas, every POI drawn with a ring and an INBOUND COUNT read from the bots' actual `brain.bb.dropTarget` (QUIET/LIGHT/CONTESTED/HOT), 12-second auto-lock, and if you never click it falls back to the quietest named zone. Spawn (player.js:356-362): `a.pos.set(p.x, 240 + rng()*30, p.z)`, `vel(0,-2,0)`. setDropTarget (player.js:421-429) then moves the human's x/z to EXACTLY the picked point — altitude untouched — so you start directly over your LZ. Chute auto-deploys at 110 m AGL the first time, 22 m after any manual toggle; SPACE cuts and redeploys freely (player.js:664-674). Firing is blocked while gliding (weapons.js:324). Landing zeroes velocity, emits "landed", no fall damage anywhere in the runtime. I simulated the exact loop at dt=1/60 from y=255, ground 12 m: passive descent 26.25 s (7.3 s freefall + 19.0 s canopy) with 24 m of drift; hold-W 26.25 s / 267 m of reach; SHIFT-dive + cut chute at 100 m AGL = 10.0 s. So the skill spread on time-to-ground is 26.3 s → 10.0 s. Bots (bots.js:379-387) steer at their target, hold mz=1, and sprint-dive inside 60 m — but they never set inp.jump in the air (bots.js:443/445/619 are all `a.onGround`-gated), so no bot ever cuts its chute. Between fights: sprint 9.6 m/s (sim/royale.js:104), no vehicles, no ziplines, no stamina; the only mobility tool is the launch portal (player.js:736-770: vel.y=42, half-gravity ascent, horizontal velocity scaled to 0.4x). Storm (sim/royale.js:260-271, half=784 m): 611 → 455 → 329 → 220 → 133 → 71 → 31 → 9.4 m over ~775 s, and each new centre may only offset by 0.8x the radius delta (sim/royale.js:339), so the worst mid-game rotation is ~281 m against a 130 s window. what_benchmarks_do: FINAL DROP (primary bar) — VERIFIED from its CrazyGames page: 100 players, building, and a published control list of "WASD movement, Space jump, C crouch, Shift toggle run/walk, M map, 1-6 items, LMB shoot, RMB aim, R reload, E use/interact (hold), P pause, Z/X/V build, B dance, N emoji, L mode select". Note there is NO parachute key in that list, which suggests an automatic descent — but its drop duration, canopy speed, and whether it uses a bus or a flight path are NOT verifiable from any public source I could reach (the official site returns almost no text, and no wiki/guide coverage exists). I am explicitly not inventing those numbers. FORTNITE — third-party physics analysis (technik-consulting.eu), not official: bus at 830 m, jump at ~810 m, glider auto-deploys at 100 m, dive-straight-down 60 m/s, angled glide 32 m/s, umbrella ~20 m/s, base run 5 m/s; effective average speed toward a target 20-32 m/s. APEX — official wiki (apexlegends.wiki.gg/wiki/Movement): no parachute at all, max skydive speed "150 (25.1 meters/second) achieved when aiming downward at an angle of less than ~15 degrees", landing pose assumed within ~30 m of the ground, and the drop HUD carries TWO meters — a 0-150 speed gauge and an altimeter with the ground height beneath you marked. Jumpmaster picks for the squad; optimal jump is ~400-500 m out from the POI. PUBG — community guides, not official: freefall accelerates to 234 km/h (65 m/s) looking straight down while holding forward; parachute auto-deploys at 300 m above the ground you are over; with the chute open and forward held you descend at 64 km/h (17.8 m/s) and move laterally at 47 km/h (13.1 m/s). WARZONE — Activision blog + esports guides: the accepted optimal descent is a deploy → cut → redeploy cadence; once you manually pull and cut, auto-deploy is disabled for the rest of the drop; forward glide is 10.4 vs 6.6 sideways (in-game units). Common thread across all four: the drop is a TRAVEL decision made from a moving aircraft, the canopy phase is short and fast, and the drop HUD is instrumented.
strengths: The drop-select screen beats every AAA benchmark on information design. hud.js:922-935 counts the bots' real declared `brain.bb.dropTarget` per POI and paints QUIET/LIGHT/CONTESTED/HOT with an inbound number inside each ring. Fortnite, Apex, PUBG and Warzone all make you guess how contested a POI is. This is a genuinely original, genuinely good browser-BR feature.

The chute model is Warzone's, correctly implemented: SPACE cuts and redeploys without limit, and the first manual toggle permanently downgrades auto-deploy from 110 m to a 22 m hard floor (player.js:664-674) — the same 'manual pull disables auto-deploy' rule Warzone uses.

The two flight modes carry a real trade-off rather than being cosmetic. Freefall is 15 m/s horizontal / -20 m/s vertical (glide ratio 0.75); canopy is 8.5 / -5.5 (ratio 1.55). Distance-per-metre-of-altitude favours the canopy, distance-per-second favours freefall. That is an actual decision, and the SHIFT dive (-34 m/s) gives a third option.
110 m first auto-deploy is a well-judged threshold — Fortnite's is 100 m. The 22 m hard floor makes a chute-cut unrecoverable-suicide impossible.
Skill spread on the drop is real and large: 26.25 s passive versus 10.0 s for a SHIFT-dive-plus-cut, measured off the shipped constants. That is a bigger delta than Apex offers.
The glide shares the ONE `moveBasis` with ground movement (sim/royale.js:145-148), so A/D steers correctly at every heading — a fixed bug, and the fix is the right kind (shared, node-testable).

Drop presentation is handled: camera pulls to 9 m in freefall / 10 m under canopy with a -0.62 rad pitch bias that points the view down at the island (player.js:1053-1062), belly-down skydive pose with banking versus an upright swaying canopy (player.js:944-957), and six seeded canopy colours so other players read as distinct dots in the sky (player.js:883).
Never-picked fallback is the quietest named POI rather than a random dump (hud.js:1163-1170 in the finish() path) — a better default than the player deserves.

The no-vehicle decision is coherent, not a shortfall. Sprint is 9.6 m/s against Apex ~6.4, PUBG ~6.3, Fortnite base run 5 m/s; the map is 1600 m, so a full traverse is ~166 s. PUBG needs vehicles because Erangel is 8 km. Last Circle does not. Do not add them.
The minimap draws the NEXT circle as a white ring alongside the live one (hud.js:1779-1783) — rotation-planning parity with Fortnite and Apex.

gaps.gap: No aircraft and no flight path — the player is teleported to a point directly above their own pick, so the descent has no destination and the drop stops being a decision
gaps.evidence: player.js:421-429 `setDropTarget` sets `a.pos.x`/`a.pos.z` to the clicked point verbatim ("Altitude is untouched, so there is still a full glide to steer"). Every benchmark instead makes the drop a travel problem: Fortnite jumps from a bus at ~810 m moving at 100 m/s, Apex's jumpmaster leaves a dropship ~400-500 m out from the POI, PUBG and Warzone fly a plane line. Ironically the bots get the better version — bots.js:98-100 offsets each bot 60-180 m from its target so it actually has to glide in. My simulation shows the player has 267 m of usable reach (hold W, no cut) and spends none of it.
gaps.recommendation: Keep the drop-select map exactly as it is, but draw a seeded straight flight line across it and spawn the player on the point of that line nearest their pick (clamped to ~250 m, matching measured reach). A far-from-the-line LZ then demands a committed dive; a near one is free. This is a spawn-position change plus one line drawn on an existing canvas — no bus model, no cinematic needed.

gaps.gap: The canopy is roughly a third the speed of every benchmark's, making the default drop a 19-second float
gaps.evidence: player.js:677-678: `const speed = chuted ? 8.5 : 15;` and `fallTarget = chuted ? -5.5 : ...`. Simulated from y=255 over 12 m ground: 26.25 s total, of which 19.0 s is canopy. Benchmarks: PUBG's open chute descends at 17.8 m/s and tracks 13.1 m/s laterally; Fortnite's umbrella averages ~20 m/s toward target and only covers the last 100 m; Apex has no canopy and dives at 25.1 m/s the entire way. 8.5 m/s of canopy travel is also SLOWER than this game's own 9.6 m/s ground sprint. A first-time player who never learns SPACE experiences 26 seconds of near-zero interaction at the head of every match.
gaps.recommendation: Raise the canopy to about -11 m/s vertical and 15 m/s horizontal (glide ratio ~1.36, close to today's 1.55). Passive drop drops to roughly 13-14 s while horizontal reach INCREASES — you lose nothing that the design is trying to protect and the umbrella still dominates the descent. Two constants on player.js:677-678.

gaps.gap: Bots never cut their chute, so an informed player always lands 12-16 s before every contestant and the drop-select heat display promises a fight the AI cannot deliver
gaps.evidence: bots.js:379-387 is the entire bot glide: steer at target, `inp.mz = 1`, `inp.sprint = d < 60`. `inp.jump` is set in only three places (bots.js:443, 445, 619) and all three are gated on `a.onGround` or on being a grounded tier-3+ combat hop. So every bot rides the 110 m auto-deploy to a 26 s descent while a player who dives and cuts lands in 10.0 s. Firing is blocked while gliding (weapons.js:324), so the bots cannot answer — they arrive one at a time at 5.5 m/s under a bright coloured canopy, into a player who has already looted. The hud.js:906 header comment sells the opposite ("it skipped the decision every battle royale opens with").
gaps.recommendation: Give the glide brain a tier-scaled cut cadence: tiers 4-5 cut at ~100 m AGL and ride the 22 m floor, tier 3 cuts at ~60 m, tiers 1-2 keep the auto-chute. One block inside the existing `if (a.gliding)` branch. HOT zones then actually mean a contested landing, and the drop-select heat map earns its screen time.

gaps.gap: No drop instrumentation — no altimeter, no descent rate, no distance-to-LZ during 26 seconds of flight
gaps.evidence: The only drop-specific HUD element is a round button reading "OPEN/CUT [SPACE]" (hud.js:1332-1334, 1604-1608), plus an LZ dot on the 180 px whole-map minimap (hud.js:1777-1783). Apex's own wiki documents two dedicated skydive meters — a 0-150 speed gauge and an altimeter with the ground height beneath you marked. Without an altimeter the player has no way to discover the 110 m and 22 m thresholds, cannot time a cut, and cannot tell whether they will overshoot; the game's single largest skill gradient (26.3 s vs 10.0 s) is invisible.
gaps.recommendation: During `W.phase === "drop"`, show a compact three-value readout beside the chute button: altitude AGL (the `agl` value already computed at player.js:660), descent rate (`-vel.y`), and horizontal metres to `W.dropTarget`. All three already exist in the loop; this is a display change.

gaps.gap: Launch portals are documented as a rotation tool but are measurably slower than running
gaps.evidence: maps.js:1047 comment: "ground launch portals at POIs: quick rotation + the way UP to islands". Simulating player.js:736-770 exactly (`vel.set(vel.x*0.4, 42, vel.z*0.4)`, ascent at 0.55x gravity, then the standard glide): entering at sprint speed and holding W gives a 72 m apex and 125 m of horizontal travel in 16.7 s — a 7.5 m/s average, against 160 m covered by simply sprinting for those same 16.7 s. With no forward input it is 31 m in 16.7 s. Two causes: horizontal momentum is cut to 0.4x on entry, and the 72 m apex is below the 110 m auto-deploy threshold so the canopy opens instantly and you never get a freefall segment. Fortnite launch pads preserve inbound velocity precisely so they read as rotation.
gaps.recommendation: Preserve full horizontal velocity on entry, and set `a.chuteToggled = true` when the boost hands over to the glide so the descent freefalls at 15 m/s down to the 22 m floor instead of opening at once. That lands the portal at roughly sprint-parity in metres-per-second while adding the terrain-skipping and vertical access it is supposed to provide. If you would rather not tune it, fix the comment — it is currently wrong.

gaps.gap: Minimap has no local zoom: the whole 1600 m map is drawn at 180 px, ~8.9 m per pixel
gaps.evidence: hud.js `drawMinimap` does `ctx.drawImage(W.map.minimap, 0, 0, size, size)` with `toPx = (x) => (x / S + 0.5) * size` and is called with size 180 — always the full world, never player-centred. The big M map uses the same function at a larger size. Circle awareness is fine; reading roads, building layout, cover or a flank line while rotating is impossible at that scale. Fortnite, Apex, PUBG and Warzone all use a zoomed, player-centred minimap and reserve the full map for the map key.
gaps.recommendation: Add a source-rect crop to `drawMinimap` so the small minimap renders a ~400 m window centred on the player (north-up is fine), leaving the M key on the existing full-map render. The minimap image, POI data and circle drawing all already exist; this is a coordinate-transform change plus a source rectangle.

gaps.gap: Mid-game rotations carry almost no pressure — circle centres are barred from moving far enough to force a run
gaps.evidence: sim/royale.js:339 caps each new circle's displacement at `maxOff = (prev.r - r) * 0.8`. With half = 784 m the radii run 611 → 455 → 329 → 220 → 133 → 71 → 31 → 9.4 m, so the largest mid-game offset available is 0.8 x 156 = 125 m and the worst rotation from the old edge to inside the new circle is roughly 281 m — 29 s of sprinting inside a 130 s wait-plus-shrink window. In practice you stroll into every circle after the first. Fortnite and Apex regularly pull the zone hard enough to force a committed, exposed run, which is where most mid-game fights come from.
gaps.recommendation: Raise the offset factor to ~0.95 for phases 2-4 only, and leave the radii and total 775 s duration alone. This moves the pressure from 'the circle shrinks fast' (which the owner already rejected) to 'the circle moves off you', which is the pressure that actually generates rotation fights. One constant, and the storm is already pure and covered by the node selftest.

verdict: Last Circle's UI is unusually deep for a browser BR — a live 3D cinematic menu, a real skin turntable, a drop-select screen with genuine bot-declared contest heat, a death recap with damage math, and a crosshair driven by the actual spread function all sit at or above what a CrazyGames-tier BR normally ships. What holds it back is not feature count but pixel-level craft and the customization/accessibility layer: four of the five gameplay canvases render at 1 device pixel per CSS pixel (soft on any HiDPI/scaled display), the big centre announcement paints over the challenge card on any viewport under ~936 px tall, the minimap is a 1600 m map squeezed into 180 px with no labels or zoom, and there is no HUD scale, no colorblind option, and no leaderboard.
what_benchmarks_do: VERIFIED about Final Drop (crazygames.com/game/final-drop, fetched this session): up to 100 players, browser desktop-only (no mobile), landscape, iframe-hosted, released June 2026, last updated 2026-06-17, 9.2/10 rating over the last 6 months, ~330 concurrent multiplayer players, and it exposes a LEADERBOARD (27 leaderboard entries listed). Its published control scheme is verbatim: "WASD = movement | Space = jump | C = crouch | Shift = toggle run/walk | M = open map | 1-6 = select item | LMB = shoot | RMB = aim | R = reload | E = use/interact | P = pause | Z = build wall | X = build floor | V = build ramp | B = dance menu | N = emoji menu | L = mode selection". The UI-relevant reads from that: SIX item slots (not five), B and N open emote MENUS (wheels) rather than firing one emote, L is an in-game mode selector, and Shift is a toggle — same call Last Circle made. Nothing below claims to know them. AAA bar (secondary sources, EA/Epic help pages and press): Apex Legends ships colorblind presets for Protanopia/Deuteranopia/Tritanopia under Settings > Accessibility, separate damage-number colour accessibility under Gameplay, and colorblind support for hit markers/hit colours; health is a white bar with shields as a blue bar above it. Fortnite ships a HUD Layout Tool that repositions and RESIZES individual HUD elements (documented by Epic for mobile; PC ships HUD scale). Warzone's HUD baseline is health bar, minimap, player count, reticle, with a kill feed that doubles as the read on who is still alive.

verdict: Last Circle's multiplayer is a well-conceived friends-only room-code mode — the slot-takeover model (humans occupy slots in a fixed 50-actor roster, disconnects hand the body back to a bot brain) is genuinely smarter than what most browser BRs do, and it means a 3-friend room is still a 50-player battle royale rather than a 3-player deathmatch. But it sits on a transport that cannot carry it: Supabase Realtime Broadcast bills 1 send + 1 per receiver, the free project cap is 100 msg/s, and a 4-human match generates ~240 msg/s before anyone fires a shot — so online play will hard-disconnect during matches, and there is no matchmaking, no invite link, no teams, no shared clock, and remote players render frozen in a jump pose.
what_benchmarks_do:
VERIFIED: Final Drop is marketed on both its CrazyGames page and final-drop.com as "up to 100 players" per match, real-time, running as an externally-hosted iframe (its own dedicated backend, not a relay bolted onto a BaaS). Its CrazyGames listing carries the "With friends" tag — which on CrazyGames means the SDK invite flow (`inviteLink()` / `showInviteButton()`, passing a `roomId` and custom params through a shareable URL) — and a Leaderboards tag. It ships dance and emoji menus as its expressive layer. NOT VERIFIED despite searching: Final Drop's bot-vs-human lobby fill, its tick rate/netcode model, whether it offers duos/squads, and whether it has text chat. I found no primary source for any of those and will not invent them.

VERIFIED on the platform side (Supabase docs, this session): free tier = 200 peak concurrent connections, 100 messages/second project-wide, 2,000,000 messages/month, 256 KB max message. Counting is explicit — "Each broadcast message counts as one message sent plus one message per subscribed client that receives it… if you broadcast a message and 4 clients listen to it, it counts as 5 messages." Exceeding msgs/s does not degrade gracefully: "connections will be disconnected if your project is generating too many messages per second," with auto-reconnect once throughput drops. Pro is 500 msg/s, 500 connections, 5M messages, $2.50 per additional million.

AAA scaled honestly: Fortnite/Apex/Warzone all run authoritative dedicated servers at 20-60 Hz with lag compensation, region-based skill matchmaking, persistent parties, and squad-first modes (Apex is squads-only). The browser-achievable subset of that is: a shareable invite link, duos/squads with knock-and-revive, a server-backed leaderboard, and a host-authoritative shared match clock. None of that needs a 60-person team.
what_last_circle_does:
Transport (runtime/net/ffg_netplay.js): Supabase Realtime Broadcast + Presence, channel `ffg:last-circle:<CODE>`, config `broadcast:{self:false, ack:false}` (no delivery guarantee, no sequence numbers, no retransmit), client declared at `eventsPerSecond: 12`. supabase-js is dynamically imported from esm.sh only when a player clicks online, so the single-player bundle stays lean. The file's own docstring line 3 reads "Turn-based online multiplayer" — this is a turn-based relay being used for a 12 Hz shooter.

Model (runtime/3d/royale/net.js): 4-char room code from a 31-char ambiguity-free alphabet (~923k combos). Creator is host = slot s0; peers sort by id into s1..sK; every unclaimed slot of the 50 keeps its bot. Docstring line 5 says "up to 8 humans" — no cap is enforced anywhere in code. World is deterministic from one 32-bit seed shipped in the `start` message, so terrain, POIs, loot spawns, chest contents and the storm plan never touch the wire.

Wire rates: own player state at 12 Hz (`now - S.lastState > 83`); host broadcasts bot snapshots at 10 Hz batched ≤24 per message, with bots >300 m from any live human dropped to 2 Hz; gunfire FX relayed at most once per actor per 90 ms (≈11/s); plus per-event messages for hitYou, chest, take, drop, emote, died, bye, takeover. Payload per actor is 8 fields: id, x/y/z (2 dp), yaw (3 dp), hp, shield, gliding flag, weapon id. No pitch, no velocity, no crouch/ADS/sprint/reload state, no rarity.

Interpolation (player.js:1021-1028): `a.pos.lerp(netTarget.pos, min(1, dt*10))` plus the same on yaw. No delay buffer, no extrapolation, no velocity reconstruction. Effective render lag ≈ 100 ms of smoothing + ~42 ms half-send-interval + network RTT.

Authority: shooter-authoritative. The firing client raycasts against the interpolated remote position, computes damage locally via `K.hitDamage`, and sends `hitYou{target,dmg,attacker,weapon,isHead}`; the victim applies it to itself. Host is authority for all bots. No validation of any inbound message — any peer can send `hitYou` for any slot with any damage, `died` for any slot, or `start` with any config (the guard is `if (t === "start" && !S.started)`, with no host check).

Disconnect: `beforeunload` sends `bye`; host watchdog fires at 12 s of silence; the slot's `netRemote` is cleared, a bot brain is attached, and `takeover` is broadcast.

Match scale: standard mode = 50 players, storm runs 8 phases totalling 735 s (~12.25 min); quick mode = 50 players, 5 phases totalling 239 s (~4 min). Movement: walk 6.0 m/s, sprint 9.6 m/s, ADS 3.8 m/s — at sprint a remote player covers 0.8 m between 12 Hz snapshots.

Social surface, in full: emote relay (reusing the local emote path exactly, so a friend's wave looks identical on both screens) and a `SYNC <n>ms` HUD readout honestly labelled as snapshot age rather than ping. That is everything. No text chat, no voice, no lobby roster (the lobby prints "N player(s) connected" while `S.peers` holds the actual names and is never rendered), no ready check, no kick, no friends list, no invite link, no rejoin.

Matchmaking: none. `NetPlay.quickMatch()` is fully implemented in the shared transport (lobby channel, two-lowest-ids pairing, deterministic room name, linger-before-untrack fix) and is never called by Last Circle. The menu's "QUICK MATCH" is a game *mode* (5-min storm, 1.8× loot), not matchmaking. The only online entry point is the "🌐 SQUAD UP" ghost button → create/enter a code.

Teams: none. Grepping team/squad/revive/downed across every royale module returns only an unused `downedAt: 0` field on the actor. "SQUAD UP" is a label over a free-for-all.

Progression: level, XP and career (matches, wins, kills, damage, bestPlacement, top10s) in `localStorage["lc_progress"]`. Local-only, no server, no cross-device, no comparison against the friends you just played with.

Message budget, computed from the above: a 4-human room at rest (nobody shooting) = host 12 state + ~12 bot-batch + 3 guests × 12 = ~60 sends/s, each delivered to 3 subscribers = ~180 receives/s, total ~240 msg/s against a 100 msg/s free-tier cap. A 12.25-minute quiet match burns ~176,000 of the 2,000,000 monthly messages — about 11 matches per month for the entire game, on a Supabase project shared with every other ForgeFlow title. In an active midgame the 90 ms gunfire relay dominates: six host bots plus three guests in firefights adds ~100 sends/s → ~400 msg/s on top, so 500-700 msg/s is the realistic figure. Even two players quiet sits at ~72 msg/s and goes over the cap the moment either one shoots.
strengths: The slot-takeover model is the best idea in the file and beats the primary benchmark on a real axis: humans claim slots s0..sK of a fixed 50-actor roster and every unclaimed slot keeps its bot, so a room of 3 friends is still a genuine 50-player battle royale with a full drop, full loot economy and a full storm. A 3-player Final Drop lobby is 3 players in a 100-player map. This is the correct architectural answer to the cold-start problem every small-audience BR has, and it is already built.

Disconnect handling is better than most shipped browser multiplayer: a 12 s host-side silence watchdog plus a `beforeunload` `bye` clears `netRemote`, attaches a bot brain to the abandoned slot and broadcasts `takeover`. No T-posing corpses, no forfeit, no dead slot skewing the alive count — the actor just keeps fighting. Many commercial games do worse than this.

Deterministic seeded world generation is the right instinct and is what makes the message-budget problem fixable rather than hopeless. Terrain, POIs, loot spawns, chest contents and the entire storm plan derive from one 32-bit seed and never touch the wire; only live state is relayed. The architecture already understands the expensive thing.

Bandwidth-aware LOD on the wire: bots beyond 300 m from any live human drop from 10 Hz to 2 Hz, and snapshots batch at ≤24 actors per message. The near-set is measured from every human's position, not just the host's — a fix that specifically protects a guest fighting a bot on the far side of the map from resolving hits against a 500 ms-stale lerp target. Someone was genuinely thinking about the wire, not just making it work locally.

Shooter-authoritative hit resolution is the correct call given there is no server tick. The firing client raycasts against exactly the interpolated position it drew on screen, so what you see is what you hit at any latency — this is the single biggest source of "this game feels broken" complaints in browser shooters, and the design sidesteps it rather than papering over it.

The HUD labels the net readout `SYNC <n>ms` — snapshot age — rather than dressing it up as ping. That is an honest label for what is actually measured, and it is exactly the kind of number that normally gets faked.
Zero dependency cost for offline players: supabase-js is dynamically imported from esm.sh only when someone actually clicks online, so the solo bundle carries none of it.

The emote relay reuses the local emote path verbatim (same `{t, remote}` shape, same clip, same hand-hide), so a friend's wave is identical on both screens rather than a divergent second system — and the comment explains it was shaped that way specifically so a later bot takeover of that slot cannot throw in `stepActor`.

gaps.gap: The transport cannot carry the game. Supabase Realtime Broadcast bills 1 send + 1 per receiving subscriber, the free project cap is 100 messages/second, and a 4-human room generates ~240 msg/s with nobody shooting (host 12 state + ~12 bot-batch + 3 guests x 12 = ~60 sends, x3 receivers = ~180 receives) rising to 500-700 msg/s in an active midgame once the 90 ms gunfire relay engages. Supabase does not degrade gracefully at that cap — it disconnects the connection. The monthly quota is worse: one 12.25-minute quiet match burns ~176,000 of 2,000,000 messages, giving roughly 11 matches per month for the whole game on a project shared with every other ForgeFlow title. The declared `eventsPerSecond: 12` is itself contradicted by the host's own ~24 sends/s baseline.
gaps.evidence: net.js: `if (now - S.lastState > 83)` (12 Hz state), `if (S.net.isHost() && now - S.lastBots > 100)` (10 Hz bots, chunked at `list.length >= 24`), `if (now - (a._fireRelayT || 0) < 90) return` (11/s per firing actor). ffg_netplay.js:43 `realtime: { params: { eventsPerSecond: 12 } }` and :54 `broadcast: { self: false, ack: false }`. Supabase docs (fetched this session): free = 100 msg/s, 200 concurrent, 2M/month; "Each broadcast message counts as one message sent plus one message per subscribed client that receives it"; "connections will be disconnected if your project is generating too many messages per second." Storm phase totals from sim/royale.js STORM_PHASES.standard = 735 s.
gaps.recommendation: Stop relaying bots. The docstring already claims a deterministic world — finish the claim: seed the bot brains from the match seed, tick them on a fixed step, and make their LOD decisions independent of the local player's position (today both player.js:626 and the net.js near-set key off per-client positions, which is what forces the relay). Every client then simulates the same 46 bots and only human state crosses the wire. That deletes the single largest term. Then fold per-event messages (fire, emote, take, chest) into the same tick as the state packet instead of broadcasting each separately, and drop own-state from 12 Hz to 8 Hz — the lerp already adds ~100 ms of smoothing, so the perceptual cost is near zero. A 4-player match then costs 4 x 8 = 32 sends/s -> ~128 msg/s, which is 3 humans inside the free cap and ~15 concurrent matches on Pro. If online play earns real usage after that, the next step is WebRTC DataChannel mesh (8 peers = 28 links, trivially fine in-browser) with Supabase Realtime demoted to signalling only — that removes per-message cost entirely and cuts latency from relay-RTT to direct p2p. Budget for a TURN fallback, since STUN-only fails for a meaningful slice of players.

gaps.gap: Every remote actor is animation-dead — they slide across the terrain frozen in a jump pose. `interpRemote` writes only `pos` and `yaw`; it never touches `a.vel` or `a.onGround`. `syncObj` picks the clip from `gs = hypot(a.vel.x, a.vel.z)` (permanently 0) and from `a.onGround`, which is initialised `false` at actor creation and is only ever set true inside `stepActor` — which `netRemote` actors explicitly skip. So the selector falls through to `else if (!a.onGround) playAnim(a, "jump", { once: true })` for every network-driven actor for the entire match. On a guest client that is all 49 other actors simultaneously.
gaps.evidence: player.js:1021-1028 `interpRemote` sets only `a.pos.lerp(...)` and `a.yaw += ...`. player.js:625 `if (a.netRemote) { interpRemote(W, a, dt); continue; }` — skips `stepActor` entirely. player.js:57 `onGround: false` at creation; the only assignments to `onGround = true` are at player.js:696 and :855, both inside `stepActor`. player.js:968 `else if (!a.onGround) playAnim(a, "jump", { once: true, startAt: JUMP_TAKEOFF_S })`. `pack()` (net.js:329-336) sends no velocity, no grounded flag, no crouch/ADS/sprint state.
gaps.recommendation: In `interpRemote`, reconstruct velocity from the snapshot delta (`vel = (newTarget - oldTarget) / snapshotInterval`) before lerping — that alone restores walk/run/backpedal selection and costs zero wire bytes. Then add one packed byte to `pack()` carrying grounded/crouching/ads/sprinting/reloading as bit flags; it is free relative to the coordinates already being sent and it fixes crouch pose, ADS stance and reload animation on remotes at the same time. Also add `pitch` — remote players currently never look up or down. This is the first thing anyone sees when they play with a friend, so it should lead the fix queue regardless of what happens to the transport.

gaps.gap: Bot damage against a guest is credited to the host. `W.reportRemoteHit` hardcodes `attacker: W.player.id` — the *local* player — but on the host it is invoked for every one of 49 bots that hits a guest. The guest's kill feed reads "<HostName> eliminated you", the death-cam locks onto the host (`victim.spectating = killerId`), and the host's kill tally is inflated on every guest's client while the host's own client shows the correct number. Both call sites have the real owner in scope and simply do not pass it.
gaps.evidence: net.js:32-34 `W.reportRemoteHit = (target, dmg, weaponId, isHead) => { if (S && W.player) send("hitYou", { target: target.id, dmg, attacker: W.player.id, weapon: weaponId, isHead }); }`. weapons.js:526 `if (W.reportRemoteHit) W.reportRemoteHit(t, dmg, p.weaponId, isHead);` with `p.ownerId` in scope four lines later at `W.actorById.get(p.ownerId)`. weapons.js:621 same omission with `ownerId` a live parameter of `explode()`. player.js:1150 `victim.spectating = killerId`. The unused exported `reportHit` at net.js:339 carries the identical flaw.
gaps.recommendation: Add an `attackerId` parameter to `reportRemoteHit` and pass `p.ownerId` / `ownerId` from both weapons.js call sites. Delete or fix the dead `reportHit` export so it cannot be wired up later with the same bug.

gaps.gap: No shared match clock — the storm is in a different place on every screen. `W.t` starts at 0 independently per client and free-runs off local rAF; the single `sync` message that carries `t` is sent once at match start and never again. Storm state is `storm.stateAt(W.t)` and storm damage is applied locally by each client to its own actors. Divergence is guaranteed and monotonic: the lobby fill animation itself advances a random 3-7 cells per 140 ms so clients leave the lobby at different wall-clock times, map build is async and hardware-dependent, and a backgrounded tab throttles rAF to ~1 Hz while each step is capped at `Math.min(dt, 0.05)` — so a tabbed-out player's clock falls behind real time by orders of magnitude and never recovers. Across 8 phases and 735 s, two players will disagree about where the wall is and one will take damage the other believes is impossible.
gaps.evidence: storm.js:72 `const st = ctl.storm.stateAt(W.t);` and :111-140 apply damage locally, skipping `netRemote`. net.js:238-244 the `sync` handler `W.t = d.t` is reachable only from net.js:276-281 `onMatchStart`, which fires once. ffg_royale3d.js:358 `if (W.phase !== "over") W.t += step;` with `const step = Math.min(dt, 0.05);`. hud.js:882-883 `const step = 3 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 5);` on a 140 ms interval, so lobby duration is randomised per client. sim/royale.js STORM_PHASES.standard sums to 735 s.
gaps.recommendation: Add `t` as one more field on the host's existing state packet — zero extra messages — and have guests slew `W.t` toward it (correct by a fraction of the error per frame rather than snapping, so the storm never teleports). Also gate the lobby exit on a fixed duration rather than a randomised fill animation so clients enter the drop phase together, and drive the fill bar off elapsed time instead of a random step count.

gaps.gap: No matchmaking and no invite link — getting a friend into your game means reading four characters aloud. `NetPlay.quickMatch()` is fully implemented in the shared transport (lobby channel, two-lowest-id pairing, deterministic symmetric room naming, and a linger-before-untrack fix for the orphaned-peer race) and Last Circle never calls it. The menu's "QUICK MATCH" is a game mode, not matchmaking, which makes the absence read as a feature that exists. Final Drop carries CrazyGames' "With friends" tag, which is the SDK `inviteLink()`/`showInviteButton()` pattern — a shareable URL carrying `roomId`.
gaps.evidence: ffg_netplay.js:86-118 `async quickMatch(timeoutMs)` — complete implementation. Grep for `quickMatch` across `runtime/` returns only ffg_netplay.js definitions and hud.js:112 `{ id: "quick", name: "QUICK MATCH", sub: "5-minute storm · double loot · hot start" }` — a mode entry. Read `?room=CODE` on boot and auto-open the lobby pre-filled; add a COPY INVITE LINK button next to the code so the host pastes a URL into Discord instead of dictating letters. That works on the ForgeFlow portal today and maps one-to-one onto the CrazyGames invite SDK if the game ever ships there. Then wire the existing `quickMatch()` into a PUBLIC MATCH button — but sequence it after the transport work, because public matchmaking multiplies concurrent rooms against the same 100 msg/s cap, and it needs the trust boundary below.

gaps.gap: No teams, in a mode whose button says "SQUAD UP". There is no team assignment, no friendly-fire suppression, no shared team UI, and no knockdown/revive loop — grepping team/squad/revive/downed across every royale module returns nothing but an unused `downedAt: 0` field on the actor struct. Friends drop into the same match and are immediately obliged to shoot each other. For the multiplayer dimension this is the largest *design* miss: playing a battle royale with friends means playing on the same side, and Apex Legends is squads-only precisely because that is the mode's reason to exist.
gaps.evidence: `grep -rn "team\|Team\|squad\|Squad\|revive\|downed\|knock" runtime/3d/royale/*.js runtime/sim/royale.js` returns only player.js:56 `downedAt: 0` (never read) and two unrelated knockback comments in weapons.js. hud.js:593 `const online = mkGhost("🌐  SQUAD UP", subRow);`. sim/royale.js `Match.prototype.eliminate` ends the match at `this.alive.size === 1` — a single-survivor win condition with no team concept.
gaps.recommendation: Add a `teamId` to the actor and to the roster in the `start` config; default every bot to its own team so the FFA behaviour of bot slots is unchanged and only humans in a room share one. Filter damage in `hurtActor` and the splash loop on matching `teamId`, tint teammate nametags and minimap blips, and change the win condition to last-team-standing. A knock-and-revive loop is the natural follow-on and is not exotic here — `downedAt` is already reserved on the actor, hp/shield already replicate, and the heal channel already implements a timed interruptible interaction that a revive can reuse wholesale. This costs nothing extra on the wire.

gaps.gap: The lobby is blind and a disconnect is permanent. The lobby prints a raw count and never the names — `S.peers` holds every peer's chosen name and is used only to build the roster, never rendered. There is no ready check, no kick, and no chat. Once the match starts there is no way back in: a refresh fires `bye`, the host hands your slot to a bot brain, and no rejoin path exists. Room codes are also unguarded against collision — two hosts can generate the same 4-char code and silently share a room.
gaps.evidence: net.js:123-127 the `peer` handler renders only `${Math.max(1, count)} player(s) connected`; `S.peers[from] = d.name` (net.js:173) is read only at net.js:142 to build the roster. net.js:157-159 `window.addEventListener("beforeunload", ... send("bye", { slot: "s" + S.mySlot }))`; the `bye` handler (net.js:223-231) attaches a bot brain and broadcasts `takeover`, with no inverse operation anywhere. net.js:150-155 `randCode()` picks 4 chars with no occupancy check.
gaps.recommendation: Render the peer list from `S.peers` — names, slot numbers, and a host badge — so the lobby looks like a lobby. Then add rejoin: persist `{room, slot, seed}` to sessionStorage on match start, and on boot with a live session offer RECONNECT, which re-enters the channel and sends `reclaim{slot}`; the host inverts its existing takeover (detach brain, set `netRemote`) and replies with a full state sync. The host already owns all the machinery for this — it only ever runs it in one direction. For codes, have the host presence-check the channel before committing and re-roll on a hit.

gaps.gap: You cannot tell your friend from a bot. `mkNameTag` paints every tag the same white on the same translucent pill for humans and bots alike, and the 46 bots carry deliberately human-looking handles from BOT_NAMES — "SweatySteve", "ClutchClara", "NoScopeNate", "SoloQueueSue". The whole point of a friends mode is knowing which silhouette is your friend, and the game does not tell you.
gaps.evidence: player.js:332-349 `mkNameTag` — `ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(0,0,0,0.45)"` for the pill and `ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"` for the text, with no branch on `a.isBot` or `a.netRemote`. sim/royale.js BOT_NAMES is a 68-entry list of human-style gamertags. Tags are additionally culled beyond 70 m (`d2 < 70 * 70`, player.js:639), so a friend across a valley has no marker at all.
gaps.recommendation: Tint human nametags (and, once teams exist, teammate tags) a distinct colour, and add a small friend chevron above teammates that survives the 70 m tag cull — the same way every squad BR draws its squadmate markers. Add friend blips to the minimap from the state packets already arriving. This is a couple of hours of work and it is the difference between "we are in the same match" and "we are playing together."

gaps.gap: Zero trust boundary on inbound messages. Any peer in the room can send `hitYou` naming any slot with arbitrary damage, `died` for any slot, `take`/`chest` for any object id, and `start` with any config — the start guard is `!S.started` with no host check, so any peer can force the match to begin. For a private friends room this is a defensible trade and the shooter-authoritative model it enables is genuinely the right call for a relay with no server tick. But it is a hard precondition on the public matchmaking recommended above: a single crafted message ends a public lobby.
gaps.evidence: net.js:191-197 the `hitYou` handler applies `d.dmg` with no bound on magnitude, no check that the attacker exists or is in range, and no rate limit. net.js:218-222 the `died` handler sets `a.hp = 0; a.shield = 0; W.killActor(...)` for any slot named. net.js:174 `if (t === "start" && !S.started)` — no `from === hostId` check. `broadcast: { self: false, ack: false }` (ffg_netplay.js:54) means no sequence numbers, no dedup and no retransmit either, so a dropped `died` message silently desyncs a client's alive set with no reconciliation path — the `sync` message covers only `t` and loot, and fires once.
gaps.recommendation: Keep the trust model as-is for code-gated friend rooms; it is the correct trade there. Before any public path ships, add host-side sanity checks on `hitYou` (cap damage at the weapon's max possible roll, require the attacker to be alive and within the weapon's range, rate-limit per attacker), restrict `start`/`died`/`takeover` to messages originating from the host peer id, and add a periodic host->guest roster reconciliation (alive set + kill counts) folded into the existing sync path so a dropped elimination self-heals instead of permanently forking the match state.

gaps.gap: Progression is local-only, so nothing survives the session socially. Level, XP and the full career record (matches, wins, kills, damage, bestPlacement, top10s) live in `localStorage["lc_progress"]` — no server, no cross-device, no leaderboard, and no way to compare with the friends you just played four matches against. Final Drop's CrazyGames listing carries a Leaderboards tag; Last Circle has no server-side persistence of any kind.
gaps.evidence: hud.js:1081-1086 `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("lc_progress") || "{}")` / `localStorage.setItem("lc_progress", ...)`, with `CAREER0 = { matches: 0, wins: 0, kills: 0, damage: 0, bestPlacement: 0, top10s: 0, timeAliveS: 0 }`. Grepping `leaderboard|achievement|registry` across `runtime/`, `index.html` and `game_meta.json` returns no integration — the only Supabase reference in the game is the Realtime relay in net.js.
gaps.recommendation: Post the post-match record to the existing FFG Supabase registry (the same project already backs games/achievements writes for other titles) and render two boards on the menu: a global weekly top-kills/top-wins, and a per-room board showing just the peers from your last match. The second is the one that matters for this dimension — a friends mode needs a scoreboard the friends can argue about, and the post-match panel already computes every number it needs.

verdict: Last Circle's audio is a well-engineered synthesizer wired to an unusually broad event set — 33 events, four-surface bullet impacts, a four-stage mechanical reload timed off each weapon's reloadS, and a real brickwall limiter on the master — but it is missing the two things that matter most in a battle royale: 3D localisation and any recorded sample content. Final Drop ships 125 recorded clips (2.59 MB total) across 219 sound components, 194 of them true 3D positional, with per-weapon-class audible radii from 200 m to 600 m; Last Circle answers with ~10 synth primitives, a StereoPanner that cannot distinguish front from back or above from below, and one 260 m radius for all six weapon classes.
what_last_circle_does: 100% procedural Web Audio SFX from four primitives (shot/blip/thump/sting) plus a siren — zero recorded SFX files; assets/audio/ contains only three music MP3s. Weapons: 6 class recipes (pistol 1400 Hz/0.09 s/0.32 gain, smg 1800/0.06/0.28, ar 1100/0.12/0.40, shotgun 700/0.20/0.60, sniper 500/0.32/0.66, launcher 420/0.24/0.56), each a noise burst through a lowpass sweeping to 20% of start, with an extra square-wave 190→60 Hz crack layer on ar and sniper only. Every shot of a class is bit-identical: one 1-second noise buffer, always started at offset 0, no playbackRate or filter jitter — at SMG 720 rpm that is 12 identical bursts per second. Spatialisation is createStereoPanner only: pan = dot(offset, cameraRight) clamped to ±0.8, gain = (1 − d/maxD)^1.4. Distance uses y but panning discards it, so there is no elevation cue and a sound directly ahead and directly behind both pan to 0.0. Fixed radii per event: gunshot 260 m for every class, footstep 24 m, chest 40 m, shield-break 50 m, impacts 45–55 m, chute 60 m, hard-land 60 m, portal 70 m, death 90 m, explosion 200 m, supply drop 240 m. Footsteps fire on a distance accumulator (2.4 m walk / 3.2 m sprint stride) as a single 300–390 Hz thump, 0.09 gain for your own steps vs 0.16 for others; walk, sprint and crouch are acoustically identical (crouch buys speedMult 0.45 and spreadMult 0.62 but no stealth). Reload is the standout: mag-release click at 0 ms, mag drop at 110 ms, mag seat at 55% of reloadS, slide rack at 86% — player-only. Music: three MP3s at 64 kbps, ~10–11 min each, 4.67 + 5.18 + 5.10 = 14.95 MB, static per phase (menu 0.9, match 0.55, endgame 0.8) with no intensity change from 50 alive to 2. Music plays as an HTMLAudioElement outside the WebAudio graph, so it never passes the limiter and never ducks under gunfire. Mix: sfxBus → master → DynamicsCompressor (−6 dBFS, knee 0, ratio 20:1, 3 ms attack, 120 ms release) → destination. Grep for Convolver, createPanner, panningModel, reverb or ambience across runtime/ returns zero hits: no reverb, no occlusion, no ambient bed. Info channel extras: an always-on screen-edge indicator ring (footstep scan at 3 Hz within 30 m, gunfire chevrons, damage arcs) and bots that hear gunshots to 250 m but never footsteps. Settings: three sliders (master 0.8 / music 0.5 / sfx 0.9). Hygiene is good: autoplay-rejection retry on first gesture, context suspend and music mute on tab hide, slider changes preserve each track's own mix level.
what_benchmarks_do: FINAL DROP (verified directly from its live PlayCanvas manifest at final-drop.games.elanrastudios.com/config.json, build 20260721.1716-99f519): 1319 assets of which 125 are audio, totalling 2.59 MB — one sixth of Last Circle's audio payload, spread across 125 clips instead of 3. 219 sound components, 194 of them positional:true (PlayCanvas positional = WebAudio PannerNode, i.e. full 3D including elevation and front/back), 157 linear + 62 inverse distance models.
