Per-class gunshot audibility, refDistance 10 m, inverse model: snipers light and heavy maxDistance 600 m, burst and red-eye rifles 510 m, revolver 450 m, assault rifle and grenade throw 340 m, SMG light/uzi/submachine and pistol 300 m, shotgun and launcher 200 m. Every weapon has fire-1 and fire-2 slots pointing at the same clip at pitch 1.0 and 1.2 (round-robin so full-auto does not sound like a loop), plus reload-start, reload-end and equip; snipers and the red-eye rifle add scope-in/scope-out (vol 0.4, pitch 0.75/0.85); the shotgun reloads with shell_insert then pump_rack. Footsteps carry stance: separate Walk entity (vol 0.15, ref 7, max 30 m) and Run entity (vol 0.20, ref 7, max 35 m, pitch 1.4), plus Swim at max 25 m. Enemy-audible actions at 20–30 m: consumable medkit and shield loops (max 20 m), chest open loops on standard/rare/mythic chests and vending machines (max 20 m), gendered damage grunts (max 30 m), Die, Consume, Health, jump voices, and emote barks ("You Better Watch It", "Defeated"). Non-positional hit feedback is layered by outcome: separate Hit_Player, Hit_Player_Head, Hit_Shield_Player, Hit_ShieldBreak_Player and mirrored Damage_Body/Head/Shield/ShieldBreak sets. Ambience and loops: Forest_Daytime.mp3, Heavy Wind 2.mp3, Underwater Cave Loop 2.mp3, skydive loop, glider loop, smoke-grenade gas loop (ref 20, max 60), storm move start/stop. Vehicles get idle/forward/reverse engine loops with per-vehicle pitch, horn, brake screech, impact, boost, ref 15/max 75. It also ships a script named uranus-input-ui-sound-clues.js, so visualised sound cues are parity, not a Last Circle advantage. AAA, scaled: Apex Legends' audio team states each weapon has at least four sound layers that change over distance, filtered with DSP EQs as the source moves closer or further and as the gun points toward or away from you, and uses occlusion (frequency modified by the density of the occluding material) plus reverb to tell you whether a sound shares your space (asoundeffect.com interview, EA audio-update blog). PUBG community documentation puts pistol reports at ~100 m and other weapons at ~200 m, with stance-scaled footstep radii (walk/crouch ~40 m, jump ~50 m, swim ~25 m, prone ~10 m) and high-frequency attenuation as the distance cue — these PUBG figures are community-guide sourced, not first-party, and I flag them as such. Fortnite's Visualize Sound Effects is an opt-in accessibility toggle with size-scaled icons and colour coding (white footsteps, gold chests, orange/red gunfire), i.e. richer than Last Circle's three fixed glyphs and, unlike Last Circle's, it can be turned off.
strengths: Event coverage is genuinely broad for a browser shooter: 33 distinct events wired, including four-surface bullet impacts (flesh/stone/wood/dirt at separate timbres and radii), prop breaks, supply-drop spawn AND landing, portal launches, hard landings, swim entry and per-stroke sounds. That is more world-event coverage than most browser shooters bother with, and more surface differentiation on impacts than I could find in Final Drop's manifest.

The reload is the best single piece of audio in the game and beats the benchmark: a four-stage mechanical sequence (mag-release click, mag drop at 110 ms, mag seat at 55% of the weapon's reloadS, slide rack at 86%) scaled off each weapon's own reload time, versus Final Drop's two-clip reload-start/reload-end. Reload progress is readable by ear, which is exactly what the channel is for.

Real mastering discipline, which almost no browser game has: an explicit brickwall on the master bus (−6 dBFS, knee 0, ratio 20:1, 3 ms attack, 120 ms release) sitting between sfxBus and the destination, added specifically so a 9-pellet shotgun blast landing on top of an explosion cannot clip in hardware.

The pan basis is mathematically correct — it projects onto the camera's right vector with the horizontal component renormalised, so looking up or down does not flatten the stereo image toward centre. The in-file comment records that this was previously the negated vector (every sound in the wrong ear at every heading); the current code is right.

Lifecycle hygiene is better than the benchmark's needs: autoplay-rejection is remembered and retried on the first real gesture rather than silently dropping the track, tab-hide suspends the AudioContext and zeroes music, and slider changes recompute against each track's own mix level so match music does not jump from 0.55 to 1.0 mid-fight.
Own-versus-other footstep asymmetry (0.09 vs 0.16 gain) so your own movement does not mask an approaching enemy — a deliberate competitive-mix decision, and the right one.

Music is real produced material rather than a short loop: three full ~11-minute tracks with distinct menu/match/endgame identities, against short 30–190 KB loops in Final Drop's manifest. The material is better even though the delivery (64 kbps, 15 MB) is not.

Screen-edge directional indicators for footsteps (30 m, 3 Hz scan), gunfire and damage direction ship on by default, so a deaf or hard-of-hearing player is not locked out of the primary information channel.

gaps.gap: No 3D spatialisation — the game cannot tell you front from back or above from below
gaps.evidence: audio.js spatial() uses `ctx.createStereoPanner()` and computes `pan = (dx*rightX + dz*rightZ)/dl * 0.8`, a dot product with the camera's right vector. A source directly ahead and a source directly behind both yield pan = 0.0. The vertical component is used for the distance term (`Math.hypot(dx, dz, (pos.y||0) - cam.position.y)`) but is discarded from panning entirely. Grep for createPanner/panningModel/HRTF across runtime/ returns zero hits. Final Drop: 194 of 219 sound components are positional:true (PannerNode). This matters more here than in most games because the map has sky islands, multi-storey structures and launch portals — 'is he above me' is unanswerable by ear.
gaps.recommendation: Replace createStereoPanner with createPanner({ panningModel: 'HRTF', distanceModel: 'inverse', refDistance: 8, maxDistance: <per-event>, rolloffFactor: 1 }), set positionX/Y/Z from the source's world position, and update ctx.listener position + forwardX/Y/Z + upX/Y/Z from W.camera once per frame in the existing update loop. Keep the current gain curve as a supplementary trim if the inverse model feels wrong. This is roughly 40 lines in spatial() plus a listener sync, and it converts the single largest category-level miss into parity.

gaps.gap: Zero recorded SFX, and every gunshot of a class is bit-identical
gaps.evidence: assets/audio/ contains exactly three files, all music. Every weapon report is synthesised in shot(): one shared 1-second noise buffer created once in noiseBuf(), started with `n.start(t)` — always offset 0, no playbackRate variation, no filter jitter. At smg rpm 720 that is 12 acoustically identical bursts per second, which comb-filters into a robotic buzz rather than reading as automatic fire. Final Drop authors fire-1 and fire-2 slots at pitch 1.0 and 1.2 on every one of its ten weapons for exactly this reason.
gaps.recommendation: Two tiers. Free and immediate: per shot, pick a random buffer offset (`n.start(t, Math.random()*0.8)`), randomise playbackRate ±10%, and jitter the filter start frequency ±8% — three lines, and it removes the machine-gun artefact tonight. Then invest in a ~1.5 MB pack of 12–18 recorded one-shots (6 weapon reports, 4 impact surfaces, 2 footstep surfaces, mag/rack) decoded once into AudioBuffers; at Final Drop's density that whole library costs less than one third of the current music payload.

gaps.gap: One gunshot audibility radius (260 m) for all six weapon classes — a sniper outranges its own report
gaps.evidence: shot() calls `spatial(pos, 260)` unconditionally. The sniper in sim/royale.js has falloff [200, 400], i.e. it deals full 105 damage to 200 m and floors at 40% beyond 400 m — so it can kill you from 300 m while its report is culled at 260 m and is already down to ~2% amplitude by 240 m under the (1−d/maxD)^1.4 curve. Meanwhile the shotgun (falloff [8,20], effective range ~20 m) is broadcast to the same 260 m. Final Drop scales by class: shotgun/launcher 200 m, SMG/pistol 300 m, AR 340 m, burst/red-eye 510 m, snipers 600 m. Distant gunfire is the primary rotation signal in a BR and right now it carries no weapon information.
gaps.recommendation: Add an `audibleM` field next to `falloff` in SIM.WEAPONS (shotgun 120, smg 200, pistol 220, ar 320, launcher 260, sniper 520) and pass `def.audibleM` into shot(). Pair it with a distance-dependent lowpass — at d/maxD > 0.4 open a second biquad whose cutoff falls from 3 kHz to 600 Hz — so far shots are muffled thumps and near shots are cracks. That gives players a range estimate as well as a bearing, which is the PUBG/Apex distance cue, and costs one extra node per shot.

gaps.gap: Footsteps carry no stance information — crouching buys no acoustic stealth
gaps.evidence: audio.js: `on("footstep", (a) => thump(300 + Math.random()*90, 0.055, a === W.player ? 0.09 : 0.16, ..., 24))` — one fixed gain and one fixed 24 m radius regardless of stance. player.js only varies the stride distance (2.4 m walking, 3.2 m sprinting), so crouch-walking emits steps at the same volume and the same audible range as sprinting. sim/royale.js CROUCH = { speedMult: 0.45, heightMult: 0.86, eyeMult: 0.60, spreadMult: 0.62 } — crouch costs 55% of your speed and returns accuracy and a smaller silhouette, but zero stealth. Final Drop separates Walk (vol 0.15, max 30 m) from Run (vol 0.20, max 35 m, pitch 1.4); PUBG community documentation puts crouch/walk near 40 m and prone near 10 m.
gaps.recommendation: Scale gain and maxD by stance in the footstep handler: crouch 0.07 / 11 m, walk 0.13 / 22 m, sprint 0.20 / 34 m, and drop the step pitch ~15% when crouching. The actor already carries a.crouching and a.sprinting. This is a five-line change that turns crouch into a real tactical decision and makes the 24 m blanket radius stop punishing careful play.

gaps.gap: Enemy actions other than shooting and walking are completely silent
gaps.evidence: In audio.js, reloadStart, reloadDone, weaponEquipped, healStart, healed and pickedUp all early-return with `if (a !== W.player)`, and `scopeState` (emitted at player.js:1093) has no audio listener at all — one of 19 emitted events with no audio handler. So an enemy reloading, swapping weapons, scoping in, or drinking a shield 8 m away makes no sound. Final Drop puts reload-start/reload-end/equip on the positional weapon entity and scope-in/scope-out on three weapons, and runs positional medkit and shield consumable loops at max 20 m plus damage grunts at max 30 m. 'He's reloading' and 'he's healing, push now' are two of the highest-value reads in the genre and neither exists here.
gaps.recommendation: Delete the player-only guards and pass a.pos with tight radii: reload sequence 25 m, weapon equip 18 m, scope in/out 12 m, heal start/complete 20 m (a looping bed for the heal duration is better than two blips — the game already knows c.useS). Add a short scopeState listener while you're in the file. All of these are close-range cues so they cost nothing in mix density.

gaps.gap: No ambience bed, no reverb, no occlusion — every sound is dry and placeless
gaps.evidence: Grep for Convolver, reverb, ambience or wind across runtime/ returns zero hits. There is no ambient loop of any kind: five maps with water, forest, and interiors all sound like an anechoic chamber between gunshots, and a firefight inside a building is acoustically identical to one in open field. Final Drop ships Forest_Daytime.mp3 (189 KB), Heavy Wind 2.mp3 (73 KB) and Underwater Cave Loop 2.mp3 (169 KB). Apex's audio team names occlusion and reverb as the two keys that let you tell whether a sound is in your space or somewhere else.
gaps.recommendation: Two pieces. (1) One looping ambience bed per map biome, ~150 KB each, mixed at ~0.10 with gain crossfading on water proximity — this alone fixes the dead-air problem between engagements. (2) A single shared ConvolverNode fed by a short synthetic impulse (generate it procedurally: 0.6 s of exponentially-decaying noise, no download), with the wet send driven by whether the player is under a roof — the world already answers that via supportAt/blockedHoriz ceiling queries. Skip material-density occlusion; it is not worth the raycast budget in a browser.

gaps.gap: Music is 15 MB of 64 kbps audio that never changes and never ducks
gaps.evidence: assets/audio/ = music_menu.mp3 4.67 MB, music_match.mp3 5.18 MB, music_endgame.mp3 5.10 MB — 14.95 MB total, all at 64 kbps / 48 kHz, ~613/679/669 seconds each. Final Drop's entire audio payload, 125 clips, is 2.59 MB. One match track plays unchanged from drop to final circle with no intensity response to the lobby draining 50 → 5. And playTrack() creates a plain `new Audio(...)` element: music lives outside the WebAudio graph entirely, so it never passes the −6 dBFS master limiter and cannot be sidechained under gunfire — during a firefight the darksynth sits at the same level as the shots it is masking.
gaps.recommendation: (a) Route music through ctx.createMediaElementSource(musicEl) → a musicGain → master, so it sits behind the limiter and can be ducked ~4 dB on shotFired/explosion with a 60 ms attack and 400 ms release. (b) Re-encode at 96–112 kbps and loop a well-chosen 3–4 minute section instead of shipping 11 minutes — that raises perceived quality and cuts roughly 10 MB from first load. (c) At <10 alive, crossfade to a tighter final-circle mix or just open a lowpass on the match track; a static score through the endgame is the single most noticeable difference from any AAA BR.

gaps.gap: No bullet whiz-by — you cannot hear that you are being shot at
gaps.evidence: The only near-miss feedback is the terminal impact sound: `on("impact", ...)` plays a stone tick at 0.07 gain / 55 m, wood at 0.07 / 55 m, dirt at 0.06 / 45 m. A round that passes a metre from your head and lands on soft ground 40 m behind you produces a 0.06-gain thump you will not register, and one that flies into open air produces nothing at all. There is no supersonic crack, no suppression cue, and no direction on incoming fire other than the HUD's red damage arc after you have already been hit. weapons.js steps projectiles client-side (stepProjectiles), so the hook exists.
gaps.recommendation: In stepProjectiles, when a live round's segment passes within ~3 m of the camera and was not fired by the player, play a 40 ms bandpassed noise crack (1.5–4 kHz) panned by which side it passed on, gain scaled by 1/(1+miss distance). Roughly 15 lines. This is the highest-value single sound you can add for the feel of being under fire, and it converts sniper fire from 'I died' into 'someone is shooting at me from the left'.

gaps.gap: The storm has no positional presence to navigate by
gaps.evidence: The storm's entire audio vocabulary is a non-positional 520→760 Hz sine siren repeated 2× on stormWarning and 3× on stormClosing, a 140 Hz sawtooth blip per 1 Hz damage tick, and a single 200 Hz thump when you cross into it (`on("playerStormState", (inStorm) => { if (inStorm) thump(200, 0.5, 0.25); })`). There is no continuous wall roar, so with the storm wall behind you or in low visibility, sound gives you no bearing on it at all — and the storm's ramping damage (+50% per 6 s soaked, capped 3×) makes getting the rotation direction wrong expensive. Final Drop ships sfx_storm_move_start and sfx_storm_move_stop. Fortnite and PUBG both use a directional storm bed.
gaps.recommendation: Add a looping low-band noise bed whose gain rises as (playerDist / st.radius) approaches 1 and whose pan points at the nearest point on the wall — storm.js already computes st.center and st.radius every frame, so the nearest wall point is one normalise away. Add a second layer that opens when st.closing is true so 'the wall is moving' is audible as well as visible.

gaps.gap: Audio settings and accessibility stop at three volume sliders
gaps.evidence: hud.js showSettings offers exactly three audio controls: Master (default 0.8), Music (0.5) and SFX (0.9). There is no separate UI/voice bus, no mono-downmix option, no dynamic-range or 'small speakers' preset, and no toggle for the screen-edge indicator ring — the footstep/gunfire/damage indicators are hard-on in stepIndicators() and update() with no setting behind them. Fortnite's equivalent, Visualize Sound Effects, is opt-in with size-scaled icons and colour coding by source type.
gaps.recommendation: Add a mono-downmix toggle (a single ChannelMergerNode on the master path — matters for anyone playing on one earbud or with unilateral hearing loss, and it is the cheapest accessibility win available), a toggle for the indicator ring, and a compressed 'night mode' preset that raises the limiter ratio and lifts quiet cues. Optionally scale the indicator glyph size by proximity as Fortnite does, since the distance data is already in hand at the addIndicator call site.

gaps.gap: Reload SFX cannot be cancelled, and impact voices are uncapped
gaps.evidence: The reload sequence is four setTimeout calls (110 ms, 55% and 86% of reloadS) with no stored handles, so swapping weapons or dying mid-reload still plays the mag-seat clunk and slide rack from a gun you are no longer holding. Separately, weapons.js emits one 'impact' event per pellet, and shotgun.pellets = 9 — a shotgun blast into a wall spawns up to nine simultaneous 2100 Hz square blips. The master limiter stops that clipping (as its comment intends) but not the phase-coherent metallic zap it produces.
gaps.recommendation: Store the reload timeout handles on wpn and clear them on reloadDone, weapon swap and death. Cap impact voices at ~3 per 50 ms window with a simple timestamp counter in the impact handler, and randomise impact pitch ±12% so the survivors do not stack coherently.

verdict: The fight itself feels good: TTK is Fortnite-calibrated almost to the decimal (AR = 30 dmg at 330 RPM = 5.5 shots/s = 165 DPS, identical to Fortnite's assault rifle), the six weapons occupy genuinely different range/burst niches, headshot multipliers match Fortnite verbatim, and the hit-feedback stack (head-priority hitmarker latch, coalesced colour-coded damage numbers, per-surface impact audio, shield-break cue, directional damage arcs) is more thorough than most browser shooters and a few shipped AAA ones. What is missing is the mechanical skill layer underneath: I verified from the shipped constants that recoil recovery (0.12 rad/s = 6.88 deg/s) exceeds every weapon's accumulation rate (AR 3.47, SMG 4.13, pistol 3.06 deg/s), so no crosshair ever climbs, and effectiveSpread carries no burst-length term — holding the trigger costs you nothing beyond losing the one-time first-shot-accuracy bonus, and the 1.14 m-diameter body hitbox on a ~0.5 m-wide character means near-misses count and strafing barely reduces incoming fire.
what_last_circle_does:
Weapon table (runtime/sim/royale.js:52-65), all figures computed by running the shipped module against a full 200 EHP bar (100 HP + 100 shield, shield-first via applyDamage):

TTK / DPS, common rarity, body shots, no falloff:
- shotgun  13 dmg x 9 pellets = 117/blast, 80 RPM -> 2 blasts, 0.75 s TTK, 156 DPS, mag 5, reload 3.0 s
- smg      17 dmg, 720 RPM -> 12 shots, 0.92 s TTK, 204 DPS (highest sustained), mag 30, reload 2.0 s
- ar       30 dmg, 330 RPM -> 7 shots, 1.09 s TTK, 165 DPS, mag 30, reload 2.4 s
- pistol   24 dmg, 400 RPM -> 9 shots, 1.20 s TTK, 160 DPS nominal, mag 16, reload 1.3 s
- sniper   105 dmg, 35 RPM, mag 1 -> 2 body shots (1.71 s + a 3.0 s reload), 61 DPS
- glauncher 95 dmg + 3.5 m splash, 55 RPM, arcing 26 m/s under gravity -18, 2.0 s fuse, bounce 0.45

Headshots: pistol/smg/ar x1.5, shotgun x1.75, sniper x2.5. Sniper head = 263 vs a full 200 EHP bar = genuine one-shot. Head zone is the top 14% of the 1.8 m capsule (0.252 m band) within a 0.20 m radius; body registration is a 0.57 m radius (1.14 m diameter) cylinder. Shotgun pellets resolve head/body independently (9 head pellets = 207 = one-shot).

Falloff, linear to a 40% floor: pistol [25,50] -> 24/24/15/10/10 at 10/25/40/60/100 m; smg [18,40] -> 17/14/7/7; ar [60,120] -> 30 flat to 60 m then 18 at 100 m; sniper [200,400] -> never falls off inside any realistic map.

Rarity ladder (+8% dmg, -10% spread per tier): ar 30/32/35/37/40, sniper 105/113/122/130/139, shotgun 117/126/135/144/153.

Spread (one shared function, sim/royale.js:152-173, read by BOTH fire() at weapons.js:400 and the crosshair at hud.js:1528 — the reticle bloom IS the shot cone). Common AR, degrees: 0.112 (ADS, still, tapped) / 0.225 (hip, still, tapped) / 0.750 (ADS spraying) / 1.500 (hip spraying) / 2.580 (sprinting) / 4.350 (airborne) / 0.930 (crouch spraying). Modifiers: ADS x0.5, crouch x0.62, airborne x2, movement graded continuously (1 + min(0.8, speed*0.075)), first-shot accuracy x0.15 when stationary (<0.6 m/s) and >0.5 s since the last shot, excluded for the shotgun.

Recoil (weapons.js:432, recovery at weapons.js:254-262): per-shot pitch kick pistol 0.46 deg, smg 0.34, ar 0.63, shotgun 1.72, sniper 2.86, glauncher 2.01, plus random yaw jitter at 0.6x. Recovery re-centres at dt*0.12 rad/s = 6.88 deg/s. Every weapon's accumulation rate is below that, so the kick is fully cancelled between shots and the crosshair never climbs.

Armour: flat 100 shield pool, shield-first, no tiers/plates/limb multipliers. Consumables: bandage 15/cap 75/3 s, mini_shield 25/cap 50/2 s, big_shield 50/cap 100/4 s, medkit 100/8 s. Healing costs 55% move speed and locks sprint (HEAL constant).

Feedback: hitmarker white 26 px/120 ms, headshot yellow 34 px/170 ms with a 170 ms latch so a body pellet cannot overwrite a head pellet inside one blast (hud.js:1812-1825); audio ping 950 Hz / 1400 Hz head; damage numbers coalesced per frame and coloured head #ffd54a / shield #6db9ff / body white (fx.js:144-160, 203-211); shield-break 1800 Hz sawtooth; per-surface impact particles and audio (stone 2100 Hz, wood 900 Hz, dirt 260 Hz, 35 ms throttle); red hurt vignette 0.7 s; camShake 0.12 on hit, up to 0.5 within 40 m of an explosion; screen-edge damage arcs, gunfire chevrons to 250 m, footstep indicators to 30 m at 3 Hz; kill banner with DOUBLE/TRIPLE/QUAD/RAMPAGE escalation.

Fire modes: SMG and AR are auto; pistol, shotgun, sniper and launcher are gated on the mousedown edge (weapons.js:322-323) so one click = one shot — but bots bypass that gate (`a.isBot || isAuto`). Bullets are real projectiles: pistol/smg/shotgun at 999 m/s (effectively hitscan), AR at 300 m/s, sniper at 700 m/s, launcher at 26 m/s. No weapon has a gravity field, so nothing drops.
what_benchmarks_do:
VERIFIED via web research:
- Fortnite assault rifle: 30-36 damage across rarities at 5.5 shots/second (Fortnite Wiki / Pro Game Guides). Last Circle's AR is 30 base at 330 RPM = 5.5 shots/s — the same weapon.
- Fortnite headshot multipliers: assault rifles 1.5x, SMGs 1.5-1.75x, shotguns 1.55-1.75x, Hunting Rifle (sniper) 2.5x (Game Rant headshot stats). Last Circle ships 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.75 / 2.5.
- Fortnite consumables: Small Shield Potion +25 to a 50 cap in 2 s; Shield Potion +50 in 5 s; Bandage +15 to a 75 cap in 4 s; Med Kit full heal in 10 s (Pro Game Guides, Fortnite Wiki). Last Circle uses the identical amounts and caps with slightly shorter channels (8 s medkit, 4 s big shield, 3 s bandage).
- Fortnite accuracy model: First Shot Accuracy (first shot 100% accurate if stationary, on ARs/pistols/SMGs) layered over bloom — random spread inside the crosshair, with "slight recoil" that players "cannot control the recoil like in CounterStrike" (Arena FPS, Kr4m, Dexerto). So Fortnite's model is bloom + FSA, which is architecturally what Last Circle implements.
- Apex Legends TTK: roughly 2.4-2.7 s to deal 150 HP on average; Warzone runs 150 armour HP as 3x50 plates and is described as low-TTK relative to Apex (PC Gamer, irnpost). Scaled to a 200 EHP bar that puts Apex around 3.2-3.6 s — i.e. Last Circle's 0.75-1.20 s band is Fortnite-fast, not Apex-slow, which is the right choice for a browser BR.

NOT VERIFIED — say so plainly:
- Final Drop's combat internals. I fetched final-drop.com and the CrazyGames page. Both yielded only structural facts: 100 players, third-person, island with weapons and resources, building (walls Z / floors X / ramps V), 1-6 item slots, WASD / LMB fire / RMB aim / R reload / C crouch / Shift as a run-walk TOGGLE, M map. No damage number, no TTK, no health/shield value, no recoil or spread parameter is published anywhere I could reach. Any claim that Last Circle's TTK is faster or slower than Final Drop's would be invented. What the structural facts DO support: Final Drop is a Fortnite derivative down to the control scheme and the shift-toggle, so it almost certainly inherits Fortnite's 100 HP + 100 shield, rarity tiers and bloom model — the same lineage Last Circle's numbers were calibrated against. That is an inference, not a measurement.
- Whether Fortnite's bloom ACCUMULATES per shot within a burst (as opposed to being a fixed post-first-shot cone). Sources describe the crosshair widening while firing but I found no authoritative per-shot curve. Treat "Fortnite punishes sustained fire more than Last Circle does" as likely but unproven.
- AAA recoil patterns (Apex, Warzone, PUBG having learnable, memorisable spray patterns) is general knowledge, corroborated only indirectly here by the Fortnite source contrasting it against CounterStrike-style controllable recoil.
strengths: TTK band is genre-correct AND well-spread. Against a full 200 EHP bar: shotgun 0.75 s, SMG 0.92 s, AR 1.09 s, pistol 1.20 s, sniper 1.71 s for two body shots. Nothing is a 0.3 s melt, nothing is a 4 s slog, and the ordering matches each weapon's range band. The AR is Fortnite's assault rifle to the decimal (30 damage, 5.5 shots/s, 165 DPS).

Headshot model is correct and honestly implemented. Multipliers match Fortnite verbatim (1.5x ARs/SMGs/pistols, 1.75x shotgun, 2.5x sniper), the sniper's 263-damage headshot one-shots a fully shielded player exactly as Fortnite's Hunting Rifle does, and the head zone is a real 0.252 m band within a 0.20 m radius after the fix that removed the full-body-width head disc. Shotgun pellets resolve head/body independently, so a blast can land mixed — the right granularity.

Weapon differentiation is structural, not cosmetic. Six weapons on five separate ammo types with genuinely different jobs, verified in the falloff table: the shotgun does 117 in one instant at 7 m but decays to ~8 per pellet at 15 m; the SMG has the best sustained DPS in the game (204) but drops to 7 damage past 40 m; the AR holds a full 30 out to 60 m; the sniper never falls off. Each also gets its own ADS FOV (20/42/45/47/48/49), its own reticle shape, its own tracer colour, its own muzzle offset and its own audio class.

The spread model is a single shared function that the crosshair reads. K.effectiveSpread is called by fire() (weapons.js:400) and by the reticle bloom (hud.js:1528) with the same state struct, so the cone you SEE is the cone you SHOOT — including crouch, airborne, rarity and first-shot accuracy. A lot of shipped shooters, browser and otherwise, draw a reticle that lies about the gun.

Stance and movement discipline is a real, legible decision worth 39x. Common AR spread runs 0.112 deg (ADS, still, tapped) up to 4.35 deg (airborne), with crouch at 0.62x, ADS at 0.5x, a continuously graded movement penalty (1.00 still / 1.20 crouch-walk / 1.45 walk / 1.72 sprint) and a x0.15 first-shot-accuracy term. That grading fixed a real defect — walking and sprinting used to cost the same accuracy, making walking a strictly dominated state.

Hit feedback is close to complete and the details show care. The head-priority hitmarker latch (a body pellet cannot overwrite a head pellet inside a 170 ms window) and the per-frame damage-number coalescing (one readable '90' instead of nine overlapping '10's from a shotgun blast) are both problems most indie shooters never notice they have. Add per-surface impact audio so you learn what you MISSED into, a shield-break cue, a hurt vignette, directional damage arcs, gunfire chevrons to 250 m and streak banners, and the sensory loop is essentially AAA-shaped.

Swap-firing is implemented correctly as a skill expression. equipSlot carries the outgoing weapon's remaining cooldown into the incoming one (weapons.js:196-200), so tap-2-tap-1 cannot double-pump the shotgun — but swapping to a second gun instead of eating a 3 s reload still works and is legitimate.

Healing now carries a cost and a tell: 55% movement speed and sprint locked out for the channel. Combined with Fortnite-identical consumable amounts and caps at slightly shorter channels, the heal-vs-fight decision is real rather than free.

A practice range with dummies that absorb, count damage and headshots, and reset instead of dying (player.js:1122-1130). Most browser BRs give you no way to learn a weapon's feel outside a live match.

gaps.gap: There is no recoil to control, and no spray penalty. Sustained fire is mechanically free.
gaps.evidence: Recoil recovery is `Math.min(a.recoilPitch, dt * 0.12)` (weapons.js:254) = 0.12 rad/s = 6.88 deg/s. Computed against the shipped kick table (weapons.js:432) and RPMs, every weapon's accumulation rate is below it: AR 0.011 rad x 5.5/s = 3.47 deg/s, SMG 4.13, pistol 3.06, shotgun 2.29, sniper 1.67, launcher 1.84. Result: the crosshair rises 0.63 deg after an AR shot and is fully re-centred before the next one — it never climbs. Separately, effectiveSpread (sim/royale.js:152-173) has no shots-in-burst term, so a sprayed AR sits at a fixed 1.500 deg hipfire / 0.750 deg ADS forever. The ONLY cost of holding the trigger is losing the one-time x0.15 first-shot bonus, a single binary step.
gaps.recommendation: Add an accumulating bloom term to effectiveSpread — a per-actor `burstHeat` that rises per shot (weapon-specific, e.g. +0.35 deg/shot on the AR, capped at ~2.5x base) and decays over ~0.4 s. Because fire() and the crosshair already read the SAME function, the reticle visualises the growing cone for free with zero extra work, which is exactly how Fortnite communicates bloom. Optionally give the AR and SMG a short fixed vertical pattern for the first ~8 rounds by raising their kick above the 0.12 rad/s recovery rate, so there is something learnable to pull down against. This is the single highest-leverage change on this dimension and it is a ~15-line edit inside one pure function that the node selftest already covers.

gaps.gap: The body hitbox is roughly twice the width of the character it wraps, so near-misses register and strafing provides almost no counterplay.
gaps.evidence: weapons.js:512 registers a body hit at `dh < K.PLAYERK.radius + 0.12` = 0.57 m radius = 1.14 m diameter, on a rig whose shoulders the code itself measures at ~0.5 m (weapons.js:520). The comment states the forgiveness was deliberately left untouched when the head zone was tightened. Consequence, computed: to make a shot miss you must exceed atan(0.57/dist), which at 30 m is 1.09 deg. A tier-5 bot in a final-circle duel against a sprinting player has an error of 0.9 (BOT_TIERS) x 1.66 (motionMul at 9.6 m/s) x 0.55 (duel) = 0.82 deg — still inside the hitbox. So at engagement ranges under ~35 m, movement does not meaningfully reduce incoming hits. The asymmetry is stark: the head zone is a tight 0.20 m radius while the body is 0.57 m.
gaps.recommendation: Taper the capsule rather than uniformly shrinking it: keep ~0.45 m at torso height, drop to ~0.30 m at the head and lower legs, and cut the +0.12 slop to +0.03. To keep bot lethality unchanged while restoring player counterplay, scale BOT_TIERS aimErrDeg down by the same proportion in the same commit. Consider widening the head band radius from 0.20 to ~0.26 m at the same time so headshots stay reachable as body registration tightens — the net effect should be that precision matters more in both directions, not that the game simply gets harder.

gaps.gap: The AR is the only bullet-travel weapon, so the mid-range mainstay demands ~2 m of lead while the pistol at the same range demands none — and bots get lead solved for them while humans get no aid.
gaps.evidence: sim/royale.js:53-63: pistol/smg/shotgun speed 999 (effectively hitscan), sniper 700, ar 300. At 60 m against a 9.6 m/s sprinter the AR needs 9.6 x (60/300) = 1.92 m of lead — about 3.4 body widths — while the pistol needs zero. Bots compute first-order lead exactly (bots.js:570, `lead = dist / def.speed`); the human gets no lead indicator, and the AR's reticle (hud.js:1661) is just a wider cross with a dot, hinting nothing about travel time. The rule is also inconsistent rather than learnable: three weapons are hitscan, two are fast projectiles, one arcs.
gaps.recommendation: Pick one rule and make it legible. Either raise the AR to ~600 m/s (0.96 m of lead at 60 m — still a skill, but a forgiving one and consistent with the sniper's 700), or give every bullet weapon a finite speed on a clear ladder (pistol/SMG 500, AR 600, sniper 800) so 'lead your target' is a general skill rather than an AR-only trap. The tracers already exist to teach it.

gaps.gap: There is no flinch or aim punch, so opening a trade confers no advantage and fights are pure DPS races.
gaps.evidence: hurtActor (player.js:1097-1133) emits actorHurt and nothing else touches the victim's aim. The only reactions are a red vignette for 0.7 s (hud.js:1449) and camShake 0.12 (fx.js:161). Because the camera lookAt re-derives from the shaken position over an 8 m target distance, the shake DOES perturb aim by roughly 0.9 deg — but that is an incidental side effect of the camera code, undirected and random, not a designed disruption. In Apex and Warzone, being hit first disrupts your aim, which is the mechanic that makes seeing your opponent first actually matter.
gaps.recommendation: Add a small directed aim punch on taking damage, reusing the recoilPitch/recoilYaw accumulators that already exist and already self-recover: roughly 0.3-0.6 deg upward scaled by damage dealt, recovering over ~0.25 s, capped so a full SMG burst cannot lift your view off the target entirely. This is maybe 6 lines inside hurtActor and it makes first-shot advantage a real thing.

gaps.gap: The pistol's listed 160 DPS is unreachable by a human, so the opening minutes of every match are fought with a weapon whose balance table does not describe the game being played.
gaps.evidence: weapons.js:322-323: `const isAuto = def.cls === 'smg' || def.cls === 'ar'; const wantFire = (a.isBot || isAuto) ? inp.fire : !!W._fireEdge;`. The pistol is semi-auto at 400 RPM, i.e. 6.7 clicks per second to reach its table DPS — at the edge of human sustained click rate. Bots bypass the edge gate entirely and fire it at the full cadence in 8-round bursts (bots.js:609-613), throttled only by a 0.35-0.75 s pause, so ~110 effective DPS versus roughly 100-120 for a fast-clicking human. Every actor spawns with a pistol (START_LOADOUT, sim/royale.js:92), so this is the weapon most early fights are decided by. The pistol also has a TIGHTER base cone than the AR (1.3 vs 1.5 deg) and is hitscan where the AR is not.
gaps.recommendation: Make the pistol's cadence honest: drop RPM to ~260-300 and raise damage to ~32-34 so its DPS lands where the table claims, or convert it to a 3-round burst on one click. Either way the printed number and the achievable number should agree, and the same table should describe bots and humans. Re-run the selftest's DPS ordering assertions afterwards.

gaps.gap: Multiplayer hit registration runs on 10-12 Hz position snapshots with no extrapolation, giving positional error larger than the hitbox itself.
gaps.evidence: net.js:286 broadcasts own state at 12 Hz, :313 sends bot snapshots at 10 Hz (2 Hz for bots far from any human — the code comment at :319 acknowledges a lerp target up to 500 ms stale). applyRemoteState (net.js:247-257) writes a bare position and yaw into `a.netTarget` with no velocity, no timestamp and no interpolation buffer. Against a 9.6 m/s sprinter, an 83 ms snapshot age is 0.80 m of positional error, larger than the 0.57 m hitbox radius. The shooter is authoritative for the hit decision (weapons.js:526 -> reportRemoteHit -> the 'hitYou' message at net.js:191-197), which correctly means YOUR shots land where you see them — the cost lands on the victim, who gets shot after breaking line of sight.
gaps.recommendation: Add velocity to the snapshot payload and extrapolate netTarget by the measured age of the last packet before rendering, which removes most of the 0.8 m for the common case of a target moving in a straight line. Keep the shooter-authoritative decision — that is the right call for feel. Worth noting this affects the multiplayer path only; the default solo-versus-bots experience simulates every actor locally and is unaffected, so this should be scheduled behind the recoil and hitbox work.

gaps.gap: The sniper reticle draws a bullet-drop hint for a mechanic the simulation does not have.
gaps.evidence: hud.js:1667 paints the sniper reticle as `dot(2); line(-1, 10, 2, 8)` with the comment 'fine dot + drop hint'. weapons.js:8-10 documents the opposite: 'Bullets fly FLAT: no weapon definition ever carried a `gravity` field, so the drop this header used to promise was never actually simulated.' The reticle teaches a compensation the player must then unlearn. Related: the sniper's falloff of [200, 400] means it never falls off inside any realistic map extent, so it has neither drop nor damage decay at any range.
gaps.recommendation: Either delete the drop tick from paintCrosshair, or add gravity to the sniper — the projectile stepper already integrates per-substep gravity for the launcher (weapons.js:483), so it costs one table field plus a tuning pass. Giving the sniper real drop would be the more interesting choice: it is the one weapon where a learnable ballistic skill would add depth without adding UI.

gaps.gap: There is no melee or any fallback verb, so an out-of-ammo player has no offensive action at all.
gaps.evidence: weapons.js:14: 'No firing while swimming (industry standard). No melee, no throwables, no building'. Ammo caps are finite (light 300, medium 240, shells 60, heavy 36, grenades 20) across 5 inventory slots (player.js:61). Fortnite always has the pickaxe; PUBG, Apex and Warzone all ship a melee. A dry player here can only run.
gaps.recommendation: Add a bare-hands or gun-butt melee on a dedicated key: short range (~2 m), ~25 damage, ~1.2 s cooldown, no ammo. This is explicitly NOT a harvesting tool and does not reintroduce building — it is purely a last-resort attack so the out-of-ammo state is a bad position rather than a dead end. Low priority, but it closes a genuine hole and the pistol GLB proto already gives you a swing target to animate against.

verdict: The map SKELETON is genuinely good — 1600×1600 m (2.56 km²) with 8–9 named POIs per map puts POI density (3.2–3.5/km²) and player density (19.5/km²) at direct parity with Fortnite (~13–18 POIs over ~5 km², 20 players/km²), and three seeded maps with guaranteed geographic biome zones, hero-silhouette landmarks, sky islands with launch portals, and a live contest-heat drop screen is a stronger feature set than most browser BRs ship. The FIGHT SPACE inside that skeleton is where it falls down: with building permanently removed, every enterable structure in the game is a blind box you cannot shoot out of (houses have one 1.4 m door, zero windows, and a 3.90 m roof against a 1.93 m max mountable height; tower upper-floor "window bands" start at floor+2.80 m against a standing eyeline of floor+1.92 m), open-ground cover averages 54–90 m between solid props, and on Isla Viva six of eight POI centres sit at or below the waterline on every seed tested — Palm Bay generates 0 of 8 houses on half of them.
what_benchmarks_do: Final Drop (PRIMARY): publicly documented facts are thin. Verified from CrazyGames: up to 100 players, third-person, "a vibrant island packed with weapons, resources, and room to build", building bound to Z/X/V (walls/floors/ramps), harvestable trees/rocks/structures for wood/stone/metal, "unique biomes", released June 2026, rated 9.2. Named POIs, map dimensions, circle timings, and interior design are NOT publicly documented — I could not verify them and am not inventing them. The one structural fact that matters: Final Drop HAS building, so its map does not have to supply cover on its own; Last Circle's must. AAA (verified via search, with a caveat): Fortnite island ~5 km², Chapter 5 playable extent ~2,600 m across, ~7 min to walk end to end, 13–18 named locations per chapter plus dozens of unnamed landmarks (one source says 9 km² — sources disagree on area). Apex World's Edge ~4 km², 15 named POIs at Season 3 launch, reported 32 POIs by Season 20. PUBG Erangel 64 km², 100 players. Design consensus from Warzone/Apex level-design writeups: POIs placed so no rotation is forced through a single choke; sightlines broken by terrain, buildings or foliage so end fights stay readable; enough cover that rotation is possible without "no man's land"; landmarks are ENCLOSED spaces where designers can predict player interaction.
what_last_circle_does: SIZE: `const SIZE = 1600` m square, 2.56 km², playable half 784 m (maps.js:23, and `half: HALF * 0.98` at the buildMap return). 50 players (MODE.standard, sim/royale.js:284) = 19.5 players/km². Sprint 9.6 m/s (MOVE.sprint), so a full 2,263 m diagonal traverse is 3.9 min; match total is 775 s ≈ 12.9 min (sum of STORM_PHASES.standard wait+shrink). TERRAIN: PlaneGeometry(1600,1600,220,220) = 7.27 m per quad — nothing smaller than ~15 m can exist in the heightfield, so terrain contributes essentially zero micro-cover. Measured relief (seed 1234, 300×300 sample): Isla Viva −7.0 to +63.3 m (70.3 m, driven by an 85 m volcano cone at 40,−60); Deepwood −3.6 to +29.3 m; Ashgrid +3.6 to +33.3 m — a 29.6 m range across 1600 m, i.e. a 1.9% grade, a plain with a d²×14 bowl. POIs: Isla Viva 8 (Palm Bay, Coco Village, Volcano Rim, Shipwreck Cove, Cliff Temples, Lagoon Docks, Jungle Market, Banana Farm, radii 90–130 m); Ashgrid 9 (Downtown Core r150, Metro Plaza, The Overpass, Container Yard, Old Mall, Crane Heights, Rubble Row, Motor Pool, Savanna Outpost); Deepwood 8 (Logging Camp, Ranger Ridge, Lakeside Cabins, Hunter's Hollow, Old Quarry, Riverside Mill, Fire Watch, Meadow Farm). Σπr² on Isla Viva = 271,000 m² = 10.6% of the map; the other 89% contains no structures at all (scatterTrees rejects `nearPoi(x,z,26)`; the only non-POI geometry is 5–7 sky islands, 4 ground portals and 130 loose loot points). BUILDINGS: three generators. `house()`/`hut()` — 4 walls, one 1.4 m door, no windows, solid collidable roof deck at y+3.60..3.90; jump apex is 7.8²/(2·22) = 1.38 m + STEP_UP 0.55 = 1.93 m max mountable, so house roofs are unreachable. `tower()` — 2–4 floors × 4 m, interior ramp through a cut stairwell hole, exterior ramp to a roof with 1.1 m parapets on the ±Z faces only; upper-floor walls span fy..fy+2.80 leaving a 1.20 m open band at fy+2.80..fy+4.00, but the standing eye is at fy+1.92, so the band sits 0.88 m ABOVE your eyeline. `tower()` is called 9× on Ashgrid, 1× on Deepwood (Riverside Mill), 0× on Isla Viva — Isla Viva has no multi-storey building anywhere. `rangerTower()` — an 11 m deck with 1.2 m rails on all four sides, the only structure in the game that is both elevated and properly covered; 3 exist, all on Deepwood. Hero landmarks (lighthouse 22 m, water tower ~17 m, steeple ~24 m, barn, silo, shipwreck hull) are all solid addBox stacks — none is enterable. COVER DENSITY, measured by replicating the generator's noise + rejection over 3 seeds: Ashgrid 318–327 solid-collider props over 2.56 km² = mean spacing 88–90 m; Isla Viva 129–141 over 0.62 km² of land = 66–68 m; Deepwood 851–867 over 2.53 km² = 54–55 m. Bushes carry NO collider (absent from propColliderKinds), so foliage is purely visual. Against that: AR falloff starts at 60 m, sniper does full 105 damage to 200 m and 40% floor at 400 m; fog is FogExp2 at 0.00042–0.00052, which at 800 m is only ~12% occlusion. VERTICALITY that works: 5–7 sky islands per map at 26–52 m with premium loot, reached by launch portals (vel.y = 42, gravity ×0.55 → 72.9 m apex); ranger decks 11 m; the Overpass deck ~9 m; Crane Heights 28 m; the volcano at 85 m as a map-wide orientation landmark. ISLA VIVA LAND: only 0.57–0.64 km² of the 2.56 km² square is above water (land is 100% inside r<200 m, 72% inside r<500 m, 31% inside r<800 m), yet six of eight POIs sit at r=484–637 m — exactly the coastal fringe. POI centre ground height across 8 seeds: Palm Bay −3.8 to +0.9, Shipwreck −4.9 to −2.9, Lagoon −4.9 to −1.8, Banana Farm −1.8 to +1.5, Cliff Temples −2.4 to +2.0, Jungle Market −2.0 to +1.7; only Coco Village (+1.2..+6.3) and Volcano Rim (+49..+59) are reliably dry. Because `town()` skips a house when heightAt0 < minH, Palm Bay places 0/8 houses on 4 of 8 seeds and Jungle Market 0/8 on 3 of 8 (approximated with the setback fixed at 12.5 m and jitter omitted) — while its road, its parking lot with 4 cars, and its 2 chests are emitted unconditionally, underwater. NAVIGATION: drop screen with per-POI live inbound counts read from bot blackboards plus QUIET/LIGHT/CONTESTED/HOT colouring and a 12 s timer; big map on M with POI names; scrolling compass ribbon; minimap; roads laid as a greedy nearest-neighbour tree over the POIs. No vehicles, boats or ziplines exist (verified by grep — zero hits).
strengths: POI density and player density are at literal Fortnite parity — 8-9 POIs over 2.56 km2 (3.2-3.5/km2) and 50 players (19.5/km2) against Fortnite's 13-18 POIs over ~5 km2 and 20 players/km2. The map is correctly SIZED for its lobby; that is the hardest thing to get right and it is right.

Three maps in random rotation, each with a guaranteed geographic biome zone that is not left to noise luck: Ashgrid splits green savanna west / desert dunes east via `(x - 40 + edge)/320` with a 120 m fbm-perturbed boundary; Deepwood has a northern snow band via `(-z - 100 + edge)/260`. Both blend with organic noisy edges rather than a hard line. That is exactly how Fortnite does biome zoning.

Sky islands + launch portals are the single best map-design idea in the build and they partially do building's job. 5-7 discs per map at 26-52 m carrying a chest + 2 floor items, reachable only by a 72.9 m portal apex, with a rim portal as the stylish exit. It is a real vertical rotation verb, a real risk/reward pull (fully exposed disc, premium loot), and it gives the map a signature silhouette.

Drop selection is better than most browser BRs: the contest heat per POI is the REAL inbound count read off `brain.bb.dropTarget` for every actor, not a fake number, with QUIET/LIGHT/CONTESTED/HOT tiers and a fallback to the quietest zone if you never pick. That is Fortnite/Apex-grade landing-zone readability.

Landmark silhouettes work for orientation. The 85 m volcano cone at map centre is visible from essentially anywhere (fog at 0.00042 leaves ~12% occlusion at 800 m), and each map gets a deliberate hero: 28 m crane on Ashgrid, 22 m banded lighthouse on Isla Viva, ~24 m steeple on Deepwood, plus a 17 m water tower on the Downtown skyline.

Ranger tower decks are textbook good design: an 11 m platform with 1.2 m rails on all four sides against a 1.62 m standing eye and a 0.97 m crouched eye — you see over standing, you are fully covered crouched, and there is an access ramp. This is the only structure in the game that is simultaneously elevated and covered, and it is designed correctly.

Cover is destructible in a way that respects the no-building rule: barrels have hp 1 and pop on any hit, trees 40-58 hp and fall, while rocks/cars/containers are indestructible hard cover. `destroyProp` zeroes the instance matrix AND kills the collider so shots and players pass through the gap. Dynamic cover without a build mode is the right substitute.

Verticality inside towers actually resolves. `addSlabHole` cuts a real stairwell over the interior ramp so upper floors are reachable on foot, and an exterior ramp reaches the roof chest — these are the fixes that separate a playable multi-floor building from a roof-only prop, and they are in.

Navigation support is complete: big map on M with POI names, scrolling compass ribbon, minimap with storm circle, supply-drop marker, and your chosen LZ crosshair while you fall. Nothing is missing here.

Roads as a greedy nearest-neighbour tree over the POIs gives legible rotation lines at zero collider cost, and towns get real street furniture (lamp posts, market stalls with loot, benches, hydrants) all flagged collide:false so they dress the space without snagging players.

gaps.gap: No structure in the game can be fought FROM. Every enterable building is a blind box with one entrance and no usable firing aperture — with building removed, the map has zero interior fighting positions.
gaps.evidence: maps.js `house()` and `hut()` emit back/left/right walls plus a front wall split around a 1.4 m door and a lintel — there is no window gap anywhere in either function. The roof deck (`addBox(x, y + H + 0.35, z, w + 0.7, 0.3, d + 0.7, roofC)`, H=3.4) collides and sits at y+3.60..3.90, while max mountable height is jumpV^2/(2|g|) + STEP_UP = 7.8^2/(2*22) + 0.55 = 1.93 m, so roofs are unreachable. In `tower()`, upper floors set `wallH = FH - 1.2` at `wy = fy + wallH/2`, so walls span fy..fy+2.80 and the open band is fy+2.80..fy+4.00 — but the floor surface is at fy+0.30 and PLAYERK.eyeY is 1.62, putting the standing eye at fy+1.92, a full 0.88 m below the bottom of the band. Ground floors have no aperture at all beyond the 1.8 m door.
gaps.recommendation: Cut real windows in `house()`/`hut()`: a 1.2 m wide x 1.0 m tall gap centred at wall-mid-height ~1.6 m on the two side walls, built the same way the door already is (two wall segments + a lintel). Add a second door on the back wall so a house has two entrances and can be pushed and held. Lower the tower band from `FH - 1.2` to `FH - 2.2` and drop it to sit at floor+0.9..floor+2.1 so it straddles the standing and crouched eyelines — this is a one-constant change plus a wall-Y offset and it converts nine Ashgrid towers and the Riverside Mill from loot closets into holdable positions. Give houses roof access with the ramp helper that already exists (`addRamp`), the way `farmland()` already puts a hay ramp on the barn.

gaps.gap: Isla Viva's POI layout is authored against an island shape the seeded terrain does not produce — six of eight POI centres are at or below the waterline on every seed tested, and two of the three towns frequently generate zero buildings while still appearing as named, heat-rated landing zones.
gaps.evidence: POI coordinates are hardcoded but the terrain is seeded, and the island mask puts the coastline at roughly r=500-600 m (measured: land is 72% inside r<500 m, 55% inside r<600 m, 31% inside r<800 m) while Palm Bay sits at 528 m, Cliff Temples 484 m, Banana Farm 495 m, Jungle Market 517 m, Shipwreck 637 m, Lagoon 632 m. Centre ground heights across seeds 1/42/1234/777/99887/20260721/5/808: Palm Bay -3.8/-0.4/-2.1/-1.0/-3.1/+0.9/+0.8/-0.3; Banana Farm +1.5/-1.5/-0.3/-0.7/-0.9/-0.5/-1.2/-1.8; Cliff Temples -2.4/-0.4/+0.4/-1.6/+2.0/+1.6/-0.2/-0.7. Because `town()` skips a house when `heightAt0(hx,hz) < minH`, Palm Bay places 0/8 houses on seeds 1, 1234, 99887 and 808 and Jungle Market places 0/8 on seeds 42, 99887 and 5 (approximation: setback fixed at 12.5 m, jitter omitted). Meanwhile `parkingLot(...)` and the two closing `chest(p.x + ..., heightAt0(p.x,p.z) + 0.6, ...)` calls in `town()` carry no minH guard at all, so an empty Palm Bay still ships a road ribbon, four submerged cars and two underwater chests.
gaps.recommendation: Add a terrain-aware POI placement pass at the top of the Isla Viva branch: for each POI, spiral-search outward from its authored (x,z) for the nearest point where heightAt0 exceeds minH over at least ~60% of a sampled disc of radius r*0.6, and snap the POI there before any generator runs. Keep Shipwreck Cove and Lagoon Docks exempt — they are intentionally coastal. Then guard `parkingLot()` and the two town chests with the same minH check the houses already use, so a POI never emits underwater furniture. Same fix protects Lakeside Cabins on Deepwood, which places 4/8 houses on 7 of 8 seeds.

gaps.gap: Open-ground cover is far too sparse for a BR with no building, and the flattest map is the sparsest. Ashgrid averages 88-90 m between solid props over terrain with a 1.9% grade, against a sniper that does full 105 damage to 200 m.
gaps.evidence: Measured by replicating the generator's noise, height function and `nearPoi` rejection over seeds 1234/777/99887: Ashgrid places 318/327/318 solid-collider props (tree 137-154, rocks 82-92, plus 36 cars, 40 barrels, 14 containers) over 2.56 km2 land = 1 per ~8,000 m2, mean spacing 88-90 m. Isla Viva 141/139/129 over 0.57-0.64 km2 land = 66-68 m. Deepwood 851/867/852 (pine 568-591, birch 204-214) over 2.53 km2 = 54-55 m — a 720-attempt pine scatter over 2.5 km2 is 0.23 trees per 1000 m2, roughly two orders of magnitude below a real forest. Bushes are absent from `propColliderKinds`, so all 113-174 of them are decoration with no collision. Ashgrid measured relief is 29.6 m over 1600 m and the terrain grid is 7.27 m per quad (PlaneGeometry(1600,1600,220,220)), so the ground itself supplies no cover either. Weapon context: `ar` falloff [60,120], `sniper` falloff [200,400] at 105 damage, fog 0.00045 leaves ~12% occlusion at 800 m.
gaps.recommendation: Everything is already instanced, so this is nearly free: raise the Deepwood pine scatter from 720 to ~2,500 and birch 260 to ~700; raise Ashgrid tree 190 to ~500, rocks 110 to ~350, and add a boulder/wreck cluster pass. More importantly, change the scatter from uniform-random to CLUSTERED — pick 40-60 cluster seeds per map and drop 6-12 props in a 10-15 m radius around each, which converts a uniform 90 m field into a landscape of usable cover islands ~40 m apart with open lanes between. Give bushes a low collider (radius ~0.9, top y+1.2) so crouching behind one actually blocks, which is what players expect from foliage.

gaps.gap: 89% of the map is structurally empty — every building in the game sits inside a POI circle, with no landmarks, ruins, farmsteads or bunkers in the space between.
gaps.evidence: `scatterTrees` rejects any placement with `nearPoi(x, z, 26)`, and every structure-emitting call in maps.js is made against a `pois[i]` anchor; the only geometry outside a POI radius is 5-7 sky islands (placed at 180-480 m from centre), 4 ground portals (placed at POI offsets anyway) and 130 loose `loot()` points. Σπr² over Isla Viva's eight POIs is 271,000 m2 = 10.6% of the 2.56 km2 map. Fortnite by contrast fills its inter-POI space with dozens of unnamed landmarks — gas stations, single houses, camps — which is the documented mechanism for making rotations interesting rather than empty.
gaps.recommendation: Add a minor-landmark pass after the POI branch and before `buildRoads`: 12-20 unnamed structures per map, placed on land at least 60 m outside every POI radius and at least 120 m apart, drawn from a small kit you already own — a lone `house()`, a two-`hut()` camp, a `rangerTower()`, a 3-4 fragment ruin using the Rubble Row wall code, a fenced paddock. Give each one 1-2 floor items and a 25% chest chance so they are worth touching mid-rotation. This is the highest ratio of felt map quality to code written in the whole list.

gaps.gap: Isla Viva has no multi-storey building anywhere on the map, so it has no interior verticality at all.
gaps.evidence: `tower()` — the only generator that produces a multi-floor enterable structure — is called at maps.js:887 (a loop of 6 at Downtown Core), :891 (Metro Plaza), :922 (Old Mall), :931 (Crane Heights), all Ashgrid, and at :1030 (Riverside Mill) on Deepwood. There is no `tower()` call in the isla_viva branch. Its tallest built object is the 22 m lighthouse, which is a stack of solid boxes with no interior. Every other Isla Viva structure is a `house()` or `hut()` at 3.2-3.4 m with a collidable, unreachable roof.
gaps.recommendation: Add three `tower()` calls to the isla_viva branch: a 3-floor stone tower at Cliff Temples (it is literally called Temples and is currently five 3-6 m cubes), a 2-floor warehouse at Lagoon Docks, and a 2-floor plantation house at Coco Village — the map's only reliably-dry town. Roughly ten lines, and it fixes the map's worst structural deficit.

gaps.gap: Several named POIs contain almost nothing — one has no structures at all — so the drop screen advertises landing zones that do not exist as places.
gaps.evidence: Volcano Rim (r=130, Isla Viva) emits four chests on a 150 m ring and zero geometry — and because `nearPoi(x,z,26)` rejects trees within 156 m of it, it is also bald of props: a 130 m named POI that is pure open slope. Fire Watch (r=80, Deepwood) is one `rangerTower()` call. Ranger Ridge (r=120) is two. Hunter's Hollow (r=100) is four 2.6 m blinds. Old Quarry (r=110) is 12 rock props plus one hut. Container Yard (r=110) is 14 containers over ~38,000 m2 = one per 2,700 m2. Rubble Row (r=110) is 16 wall fragments spread over ±93 m = mean spacing ~46 m, too sparse to function as the cover playground its own code comment calls it. The Overpass (r=120) is five pillars and a deck with no interior of any kind.
gaps.recommendation: Set a floor of roughly 6-8 collidable structures per named POI and audit against it. Concretely: give Volcano Rim a ring of collapsed obsidian slabs plus a 2-floor observatory on the rim (it is the map's centrepiece and currently the worst POI in the game); triple Container Yard to ~40 containers and stack them two high with connecting ramps so it becomes the vertical CQB maze the name promises; double Rubble Row to ~35 fragments and cluster them into 5-6 defensible knots rather than uniform scatter; add a station building and a stairwell to The Overpass.

gaps.gap: Hero landmarks are solid props, not playable space — the most memorable silhouettes on each map are the ones you cannot enter.
gaps.evidence: `lighthouse()` is six stacked solid `addBox` bands plus a light room; `steeple()` is `addBox(x, y+4, z, 8, 8, 11)` for the church body — a solid 8x8x11 m block — plus a solid bell tower and spire; `farmland()`'s barn is `addBox(bx, by+2.4, bz, 8, 4.8, 12)`, solid, with only a hay ramp to a roof chest; the silo, the water tower tank and the Isla Viva shipwreck hull are all solid boxes. None has a hollow interior. The documented AAA principle is the opposite — landmarks are valued precisely because they are ENCLOSED spaces where designers can predict player interaction.
gaps.recommendation: Hollow the three landmarks that most want it, reusing the wall-with-door-gap pattern `hut()` already implements: the church (a nave with a door at each end and a bell-tower ladder ramp to a 24 m sniper perch), the barn (a two-level interior with a hayloft, keeping the existing roof ramp), and the lighthouse (a spiral of `addRamp` segments to the 22 m light room). Each becomes a genuine destination rather than a navigation beacon.

gaps.gap: Six of the ~25 POIs across all three maps come out of the same `town()` generator and two more out of the same `farmland()` generator, differing only in roof colour and house count — so most POIs are not visually distinguishable from each other on approach.
gaps.evidence: `town()` builds Palm Bay, Coco Village and Jungle Market on Isla Viva, Savanna Outpost on Ashgrid, and Logging Camp and Lakeside Cabins on Deepwood; the only per-call variation is `wallCs`, `roofC`, `along` ('x' or 'z') and `nPer` (4 or 5). `farmland()` builds Banana Farm and Meadow Farm with identical geometry. That is 8 of 25 POIs from 2 generators. Beyond the single hero landmark each map receives, there is no per-POI silhouette differentiation.
gaps.recommendation: Give `town()` a layout parameter beyond the axis: a crossroads variant (two perpendicular streets), a plaza variant (houses ringing an open square with a central well or monument), and a terraced variant (houses stepped up a slope) — the existing house-placement loop supports all three with different a0/set functions. Then give each town one signature structure it alone has (a market hall, a fuel depot, a clocktower) so it reads as itself at 300 m.

gaps.gap: Terrain contributes no cover at any scale a player can use — 7.27 m per heightfield quad means there are no ditches, berms, gullies or reverse slopes anywhere.
gaps.evidence: `const SEG = 220` over `SIZE = 1600` gives 7.27 m per quad, so the smallest representable feature is ~15 m across and heavily smoothed by `computeVertexNormals`. The height functions compound this: Ashgrid's finest octave is `fbm(x/40, z/40, seed+7, 2, 2.0, 0.5) * 1.6` — a maximum 1.6 m of 'rubble roughness'. Measured relief is 29.6 m on Ashgrid, 33.0 m on Deepwood, both across the full 1600 m span. Combined with the 88-90 m prop spacing on Ashgrid, a player crossing open ground there has literally nothing to break line of sight for a 9.4 s sprint.
gaps.recommendation: Two cheap changes. Raise SEG from 220 to 320 (7.27 m -> 5.0 m per quad, ~2.1x vertex count on a plane that is already the cheapest mesh in the scene) and add a high-frequency ridged octave to each height function — something like `+ (0.5 - Math.abs(fbm(x/28, z/28, seed+9, 2, 2, 0.5) - 0.5)) * 5` — which produces 2-4 m gullies and berms at a scale a prone or crouched player can actually use. Do it on Ashgrid first: it is the flattest map and gains the most.

gaps.gap: Chest world-Y is computed at the POI CENTRE while the chest is placed at an offset of up to half the POI radius, so on any sloped POI chests float in the air or sink into the ground.
gaps.evidence: The pattern `chest(p.x + (rng() - 0.5) * p.r, heightAt0(p.x, p.z) + 0.6, p.z + (rng() - 0.5) * p.r, p.id)` appears in the Container Yard, Rubble Row and `farmland()` blocks, and `town()` closes with `chest(p.x + (rng() - 0.5) * R * 0.6, heightAt0(p.x, p.z) + 0.6, p.z + (rng() - 0.5) * R * 0.6, p.id)`. With Isla Viva relief at 70 m and POI radii of 90-130 m, a chest placed 40 m from the POI centre can easily be several metres off the real ground. On Isla Viva's submerged POIs it also puts chests underwater.
gaps.recommendation: Replace `heightAt0(p.x, p.z)` with the chest's own sampled ground in all four call sites — compute the offset x/z first, then `heightAt0(cx, cz) + 0.6`. Add a `if (gy < waterY + 0.5) continue;` guard so no chest spawns in the sea. Five-line fix, four sites.

gaps.gap: No cross-map traversal tool exists other than sprinting and swimming, which is a specific problem on Isla Viva where 76% of the square is ocean.
gaps.evidence: Grepping the whole runtime for vehicle, zipline, boat, jumppad and launchpad returns zero hits — the only mobility verbs are MOVE.walk 6.0, MOVE.sprint 9.6, MOVE.swim 4.0, MOVE.swimSprint 5.6 and the launch portals. Measured Isla Viva land is 0.57-0.64 km2 of the 2.56 km2 map, and its coastal POIs sit 484-637 m from centre, so lateral movement between them either detours inland or crosses water at 42-58% of sprint speed. Compounding this, the storm's `radiusFrac` is applied to `W.map.half` with no knowledge of water, so an identical circle schedule squeezes players onto far less usable ground on Isla Viva than on the other two maps.
gaps.recommendation: Skip vehicles — they are a large scope item and a physics/netcode risk. Add ziplines instead: they cost roughly what a portal costs, they already fit the launch-portal aesthetic, and they solve exactly this problem. Run 4-6 per map between POI pairs that the road graph already connects (the greedy NN tree gives you the pairs for free), plus 2-3 on Isla Viva spanning water. Separately, on water maps bias the storm circle centres toward land: when generating each circle, sample ~20 points in the candidate disc and reject centres where under half are above waterY — measured over 300 seeds, 4% of Isla Viva matches currently end with the final circle under 50% land and 9 of 300 end with it entirely in the sea.

verdict: Everything a player sees once they are in the match is genuinely good — the auto-opening how-to card, the contested-LZ drop screen, the pistol-on-spawn rule and a dense, correct HUD put Last Circle ahead of what Final Drop's own store page documents. The problem is everything before that: measured from the code's own constants, a first-time player stares at a blank dark page, then a menu, then a loading screen, then an unskippable 4.0 s lobby, then a 12 s map screen, then a 25.3–26.8 s parachute ride — roughly 45–70 seconds from opening the page to the first trigger pull, in the mode the game presents first.
what_benchmarks_do: VERIFIED (CrazyGames developer docs, the platform Final Drop ships on): "Games should land new users in gameplay immediately. If this is not feasible given the game specifics, a maximum of 1 click is allowed." Launch metrics: goal "load in under 10 seconds", "build size below 20 MB", "Top-performing titles typically convert 80%+ of players", "Successful titles often see 10+ minutes of average play time", "Strong games often achieve 10-15% Day 1 Retention". Loading doc thresholds: "<100 ms — perceived as instant", "1 second — feels fine, does not break flow", "10 seconds — attention starts to wander. You must show feedback or preload activities"; load time is measured "up to the moment your game calls the SDK gameplayStart method"; recommended strategy is load tutorial-critical assets first, start gameplay, stream the rest in background. Gameplay requirements also mandate mobile: content readable at 800x450 and "intuitive controls on different types of devices". VERIFIED (Final Drop): up to 100 players, browser-instant, controls WASD / LMB shoot / RMB aim / Z-X-V build / M map / 1-6 items / R reload / E interact; its CrazyGames listing documents NO tutorial and no onboarding sequence — only a controls list and a prose tip ("Look for small clusters of houses on the edges of the map"). UNVERIFIED: Final Drop's actual boot time, lobby wait, parachute duration and whether its lobbies are bot-filled — no public source states these, and I did not play it. VERIFIED (Apex Legends): "All players are required to complete training before they can play any other game mode"; new players stay in protected matchmaking until they "place in the top five of the battle royale or complete enough of the challenges". UNVERIFIED: Fortnite's exact skydive/glider auto-deploy height and total drop duration — searches returned only qualitative guidance, no numbers, so I am not asserting any.
what_last_circle_does: MEASURED LIVE (served locally, Chrome, three.js warm in cache — a cold real-network run is worse, not better): DOM ready 646 ms; the last boot module (content.json) resolves at 2,177 ms and the menu paints right after; 42 requests to reach an interactive menu. three.js is pulled from cdn.jsdelivr.net as 16 chained requests totalling ~1.5 MB decoded (three.module.js 562 KB + three.core.js 737 KB + 210 KB of addons). music_menu.mp3 is fetched in full the moment the menu appears: 4,785 KB, start 2,540 ms, end 3,198 ms. Match start pulls the cast: 48 GLB requests, 7,554 KB decoded, 2,604 ms on a zero-latency localhost. buildMap is fast — isla_viva 701 ms (cold, includes procedural texture generation), ashgrid 571 ms, deepwood 302 ms — and 50 skeleton clones cost 23 ms total. FROM THE CODE: index.html is 14 lines with no loading markup and background #08131f; ffg_boot3d.js top-level-awaits the kernel and genre modules on lines 12-13, OUTSIDE the try/catch on line 21. showLobby fills 50 cells at 140 ms ticks of 3-8, then counts 3-2-1 at 900 ms = ~4.0 s, with no skip handler. showDropSelect runs a 12 s auto-lock timer (skippable via the DROP button). Glide constants in player.js: spawn y = 240 + rng()*30, freefall lerps to -20 m/s (-34 sprinting), chute auto-deploys at 110 m AGL, canopy descends at -5.5 m/s. Integrating that math exactly: 25.3 s from y=240 and 26.8 s from y=270 with no input; 14.5 s if the player cuts the chute with SPACE; 9.3 s cut + sprint. START_LOADOUT = pistol, rarity 0, 36 light ammo — everyone lands armed. MODE.quick = ground drop, startRadiusFrac 0.75, lootMult 1.8, 25 starting shield, storm phase 1 wait 30 s (vs standard's 80 s), i.e. no glide gap at all. STORM_PHASES.standard phase 1 = wait 80 s before anything closes, so nothing storm-related happens in the first 60 s. BOT_TIER_MIX.standard = [8,12,14,10,5] over 49 bots, fixed — nothing reads W.progress.level, so a first-ever match contains ~5 tier-5 bots (210 ms reaction, 0.9° aim error) and ~10 tier-4 (300 ms, 1.8°). The first-run HOW TO PLAY modal is gated on localStorage "lc_seen_intro" and auto-opens 500 ms after the menu — I confirmed it live: the modal was present on a fresh profile with all 11 control rows rendered. Total shipped assets: 11.4 MB of GLB + 15.0 MB of audio (three ~5 MB mp3s).
strengths: One click from menu to match. Each mode card IS the play button (c.onclick -> startMatch({mapId: randomMap(), mode: m.id})) — there is no separate DROP IN step. That meets CrazyGames' literal requirement: 'a maximum of 1 click is allowed.'

A first-run onboarding card exists and fires unprompted — hud.js line ~602: if (!localStorage.getItem('lc_seen_intro')) setTimeout(() => showHowToPlay(W), 500). Verified live on a clean profile. It covers 11 verbs including the two nobody would guess (C crouch, B/N emotes) and explains the reticle bloom. Final Drop's CrazyGames listing documents no tutorial of any kind, so this is a lead over the primary benchmark, not parity.
Zero matchmaking wait, structurally. The lobby is 49 bots registered synchronously in _startMatch — there is no queue that can ever be empty at 3am. A 100-player real-lobby BR cannot promise that.

The drop-select screen is the real thing, not a decoration. Contest heat is computed from bots' actual declared targets (a.brain.bb.dropTarget, set by bots.assignDrops before the lobby), rendered as a per-POI inbound count inside the ring with a QUIET/LIGHT/CONTESTED/HOT legend, and a no-pick fallback that lands you at the QUIETEST named zone rather than a random dump. This is the genre's signature opening decision, implemented honestly.

Everyone spawns armed. START_LOADOUT = pistol + 36 light ammo means the moment your feet touch ground you can fight — there is no naked-scavenger phase, which is exactly the right call for a session that has already spent 30 seconds on descent.

The in-match HUD is legible and complete for a first-timer: hp/shield bars with the percentage inside, hp recolouring and pulsing below 25, a compass ribbon, a 10 Hz minimap with storm rings, a storm clock labelled 'shrinks'/'closing' rather than a bare number, alive and kill counters, kill feed, screen-edge directional indicators for gunfire/footsteps/damage, '[E] Assault Rifle' and '[HOLD E] Open chest' prompts, a reload progress bar, a sprint-latch pip, and a per-weapon reticle sized off the real effectiveSpread() call rather than a guess.
The drop itself is taught in-world: the chute button reads 'CUT [SPACE]' or 'OPEN [SPACE]' live, and a DEPLOY announcement fires 250 ms into the match ('50 PLAYERS · LAST ONE STANDING WINS').

Map generation is genuinely fast — 302 to 701 ms measured across all three maps, including procedural terrain (220x220 segments), structures and canvas PBR textures. The loading screen is not hiding a slow generator; it is hiding a download.
Practice mode is a real practice mode, not a label: five dummies at exactly 12/22/35/55/80 m due south of spawn, a full loadout, and a live 'SHOTS / HITS / ACC / HEADSHOTS / DMG / DOWNS' readout.

Settings clears the accessibility bar most browser games do not: FOV 50-85, separate hip and ADS sensitivity with a hard floor so the slider cannot brick mouse-look, hold-vs-toggle for both sprint and ADS, full keybind remap that refuses conflicting binds instead of silently stealing them, three graphics tiers, and an opt-in FPS readout so 'is it me or the game' has an answer.

The retention loop is wired: the menu shows LVL, an XP bar, a career line (matches/wins/kills/best placement) and the next skin unlock, and PLAY AGAIN requeues straight into a fresh match without rebuilding the cinematic menu world or re-reading the skin GLBs.

gaps.gap: Nothing on screen between the first byte and the menu — no logo, no spinner, no progress, no error path
gaps.evidence: index.html is 14 lines and contains only <div id="game-container"> over background #08131f. ffg_boot3d.js awaits the kernel + genre modules at top level (lines 12-13), which in turn pull three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net as 16 chained requests (~1.5 MB decoded) plus ten local runtime modules and content.json. Measured with three.js already warm in cache: content.json resolves at 2,177 ms and the menu paints after that. Cold, on a real connection, that flat dark rectangle is materially longer. CrazyGames' own loading doc: '10 seconds — attention starts to wander. You must show feedback or preload activities.'
gaps.recommendation: Put a static splash directly in index.html — wordmark, a determinate bar, and a one-line tip — that paints on the first frame with zero JS, and have showMenu remove it. Free bytes, and it converts the worst part of the funnel from 'is this broken?' into 'it's loading.'

gaps.gap: Time from clicking PLAY to the first trigger pull is ~45-70 s in the mode the game presents first
gaps.evidence: Summing the code's own constants: character assets 7,554 KB across 48 GLB requests (measured 2,604 ms on zero-latency localhost, realistically 4-10 s on a home connection) + showLobby's fill-then-3-2-1 = ~4.0 s with no skip handler + showDropSelect's 12 s auto-lock + a parachute descent I integrated straight from player.js constants (spawn y 240-270, freefall lerp to -20 m/s, chute auto-deploys at 110 m AGL, canopy -5.5 m/s) at 25.3-26.8 s with no input. The storm's first phase does not even begin for 80 s, so the entire first minute is transit.
gaps.recommendation: Attack the three cheapest segments in order: make the 4.0 s lobby click-to-skip (nothing is loading during it — the roster was built before showLobby was called), let ENTER or a click on the map finish drop-select instantly, and shorten the descent (next item). Getting to ~25 s total is achievable without removing a single feature.

gaps.gap: The parachute owns 110 m of a ~240 m descent at 5.5 m/s — the slowest speed in the game — and nothing teaches the new player to cut it
gaps.evidence: player.js: `if (!a.chute && agl < (a.chuteToggled ? 22 : 110)) deployChute(W, a)` with `fallTarget = chuted ? -5.5 : ...`. Integrating: 25.3 s from y=240, 26.8 s from y=270 with no input; 14.5 s if the player cuts the chute; 9.3 s cut + sprint. The HOW TO PLAY card's SPACE line reads 'Jump · re-open the parachute in a long fall' — that describes redeploy, not the cut that halves the ride. The in-air 'CUT [SPACE]' button is correct but appears on the one screen where a first-timer is watching the ground, not the corner.
gaps.recommendation: Drop the first-time auto-deploy from 110 m to ~60 m — the default descent falls to roughly 15-17 s while the freefall feel, the steering and the glide are all untouched. Then change the how-to line to 'SPACE — cut the chute to dive faster, tap again to re-open.'

gaps.gap: QUICK MATCH already is the fast onboarding path, and nothing tells the player that
gaps.evidence: MODE.quick = ground drop (no glide, no drop-select), startRadiusFrac 0.75 (pre-shrunk), lootMult 1.8, 25 shield at spawn, storm phase 1 in 30 s vs standard's 80 s. So it skips the entire ~38 s of lobby-to-ground transit that standard imposes. But it sits second under BATTLE ROYALE and its subtitle reads '5-minute storm · double loot · hot start' — a variant, not a starting point. A first-time visitor clicks the top card.
gaps.recommendation: On a profile with zero recorded matches (W.progress.career.matches === 0), promote QUICK MATCH to the top card, badge it 'START HERE — FIGHTING IN 10 SECONDS', and let BATTLE ROYALE take second. Zero new systems; it is a sort order and a string.

gaps.gap: No touch input of any kind — a mobile visitor gets a tappable menu and then an unplayable match
gaps.evidence: grep for touchstart|touchmove|ontouchstart|maxTouchPoints|isMobile across runtime/, game_controls.js and index.html returns exactly one hit: `window.addEventListener("pointerdown", unlock)` in audio.js, an autoplay unlock. Movement, look, fire, ADS, reload, loot, weapon-swap and the chute are keyboard/mouse only. CrazyGames' gameplay requirements state the game 'should have intuitive controls on different types of devices' and that content must be readable at 800x450.
gaps.recommendation: If mobile is in scope, this outranks every other item here because it is a 100% failure rate for that segment: left virtual stick, right look-drag, a fire button, and taps on the existing chute/interact/slot widgets. If mobile is explicitly out of scope, then detect touch at boot and show a one-line 'Last Circle needs a keyboard and mouse' card instead of a match the player cannot move in.

gaps.gap: A 4.79 MB menu music file downloads the instant the menu appears and competes with everything else in the funnel
gaps.evidence: Measured: music_menu.mp3, 4,785 KB, request start 2,540 ms, complete 3,198 ms — on localhost. It begins the moment showMenu calls startMenuMusic, i.e. exactly while the player is deciding which card to click, and it will still be in flight when the match's 7.5 MB of characters starts. The three tracks total 15.0 MB against 11.4 MB of GLB; CrazyGames' launch bar is 'build size below 20 MB' and 'load in under 10 seconds'.
gaps.recommendation: Re-encode the three tracks to ~96 kbps mono loops (5 MB -> under 1 MB each) and hold the fetch until either the first user gesture or an idle callback, so the menu track never races the match assets for the same connection pool.

gaps.gap: The engine is a third-party CDN dependency with no fallback and no visible error path
gaps.evidence: The importmap in index.html points three and three/addons/ at cdn.jsdelivr.net, and ffg_boot3d.js awaits those imports at top level on lines 12-13 — outside the try/catch that starts on line 21. If jsdelivr is blocked (school and corporate networks routinely do this) or slow, the module throws before any handler exists: the player sees the flat #08131f rectangle forever, with a console.error they will never open. A local copy of the library already exists in the repo at forgeflow-games/three172.js.
gaps.recommendation: Self-host three from the game's own origin, or keep the CDN as primary with a same-origin fallback specifier — and wrap the boot imports so a failure paints 'Could not load the game engine. Reload?' instead of nothing.

gaps.gap: First-ever match puts the player against the full skill spread with no protection
gaps.evidence: BOT_TIER_MIX.standard = [8,12,14,10,5] over 49 bots and nothing reads W.progress.level or career.matches — bots.js draws the tier purely from the seeded mix. So match one contains roughly 5 tier-5 bots (BOT_TIERS: 210 ms reaction, 0.9 deg aim error) and 10 tier-4 (300 ms, 1.8 deg). Apex, by contrast, requires training before any other mode and keeps new accounts in protected matchmaking until they place top five or clear challenges.
